definition_zh: 亲自；本人；就个人而言；针对个人地；以个人身份
definition_en: in your own person rather than through someone else, or as your own opinion
core_image: 一个人把袖口挽起，自己伸手去搬那只箱子，不叫别人代劳
scene: 会议开到一半，负责人放下笔，环视一圈，表示这件事他要自己去做，不转交别人。I will personally check every page before it goes out.
sceneCN: 这里是「亲自、本人」（第 1 个义项：不假手他人，由当事人自己做）；句意为每一页在发出去之前他都要亲自核对。画面里是他卷起袖子自己动手的样子。

pos.zh: 亲自；本人；就个人而言；针对个人地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「个人的；私人的」
同族名词，来自拉丁语 persona，义为「人」
由否定前缀 im- 加 personal 构成，义为「非个人的；没有人情味的」

senses.title: In your own person, not through another
senses.definition: done by you yourself rather than by someone acting for you
senses.definitionCN: 由你本人去做，而不是由替你办事的人去做
senses.example: The manager personally handed each worker a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 经理亲自把信交到每位工人手里。
senses.why: The adverb simply turns the adjective into a manner: in the manner of the person himself, with no stand-in in between.
senses.whyCN: 副词只是把形容词变成方式状语：以本人的方式去做，中间不隔一个代办的人。

senses.title: As my own opinion
senses.definition: used to mark a statement as your own view rather than as a general fact
senses.definitionCN: 用来表明某句话只是你自己的看法，而不是普遍事实
senses.example: Personally, I would wait another week before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 就我个人而言，我会再等一周才作决定。
senses.why: If the word points to the speaker in person, it can also point to that speaker's private judgement as against what everyone says.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指向说话人本人，它也能指向这个人自己的判断，与大家普遍的说法相对，于是有了发表私见的用法。

senses.title: As an attack on oneself
senses.definition: in a way that feels aimed at you as a person rather than at what you did
senses.definitionCN: 以一种让人感到是冲着你这个人、而不是针对你所做之事的方式
senses.example: She took the criticism personally and stopped speaking to us.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那句批评当成了针对自己，从此不再和我们说话。
senses.why: To take something personally is to move the remark from the work to the worker, and the adverb marks exactly that shift.
senses.whyCN: 把一句话当成针对个人，就是把评价从事情挪到人身上，副词正是标明这一挪动发生在哪里。

senses.title: As an individual, in one's own right
senses.definition: in your own individual capacity, especially when responsibility or blame is assigned
senses.definitionCN: 以你个人的身份，尤用于责任或过失的归属
senses.example: He is personally liable for the damage caused by the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这台机器造成的损失负有个人责任。
senses.why: Legal and official writing needs to separate a role from the person filling it, so the adverb pins responsibility on the individual body.
senses.whyCN: 法律与公文需要把职位和坐在职位上的人分开，副词就把责任钉在具体这个人身上。

intro.en: Personally is an English formation: the adjective personal, itself from Latin persona, plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: personally 是英语自己构成的词：形容词 personal（源自拉丁语 persona）加上副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Persona meant a mask and the role it marked; its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: persona 意为面具以及面具所标示的角色；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Late Latin personalis meant belonging to a person and reached English through French as personal.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 personalis 意为属于某个人的，经法语以 personal 的形式进入英语。

items.en: Middle English had the adjective personal but no settled adverb, and writers used phrases such as in person instead.
items.cn: 中古英语已有形容词 personal，却没有定型的副词，人们多用「以本人身份」一类短语。

items.en: Adding the native suffix -ly to personal produced personally, following the usual adjective-to-adverb pattern.
items.cn: 在 personal 后加英语本族后缀 -ly，按形容词变副词的常规路子构成了 personally。

items.en: By the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries personally also marks a speaker's own opinion and, in law, individual liability.
items.cn: 到十八、十九世纪，personally 又用来标记说话人自己的看法，并在法律中指个人责任。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective this adverb was built from; the near-meaning group collects words for doing something oneself.
note.cn: 形近组收构成这个副词的名词与形容词；近义组收表示本人亲自做某事的词。

entries.definition: The adjective the adverb was built from, meaning of one person or private.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的原形容词，意为个人的或私人的。

entries.definition: A single human being, the noun at the bottom of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 一个单独的人，是这一族词最底层的名词。

entries.definition: The qualities that make one person different from another.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个人区别于他人的那些特质。

entries.definition: In a way that shows no feeling for the individual involved.
entries.definitionCN: 以不关心具体某个人的方式。

entries.definition: Present yourself rather than sending someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 本人到场，而不是派人或送东西去。

entries.definition: Without any person or thing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 中间不经过任何人和物。

entries.definition: Used to stress that a person acts without help.
entries.definitionCN: 用来强调某人无需他人帮助地行动。

entries.definition: In a way that is not public and not shared.
entries.definitionCN: 以不公开、不与人分享的方式。

normalIntro.en: The adverb is personal plus a native ending, and it keeps the whole range of the noun person inside one word.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词就是 personal 加一个本族词尾，把「人」这个名词的全部跨度收进了一个词里。

normal.en: Personally is personal plus -ly, the ordinary English way of turning an adjective into an adverb of manner.
normal.cn: personally 就是 personal 加 -ly，是英语把形容词变成方式副词最普通的方式。

normal.en: The same ending that gives personally also gives quickly, so the pattern carries over without effort.
normal.cn: 构成 personally 的这个词尾也能构成 quickly，所以这个模式可以毫不费力地套用。

normal.en: In person and personally both stress the body of the person, but only the adverb can also mean in my opinion.
normal.cn: in person 与 personally 都强调本人的身体，但只有副词还能表示在我看来。

normal.en: Take it personally is almost always negative: the remark was about the work, and the listener heard it about the self.
normal.cn: 把它当成针对自己几乎总是负面的：话本来说的是工作，听的人却听成了说自己。

normal.en: In contracts, personally liable fixes blame on the human being behind the company name.
normal.cn: 在合同里，负有个人责任把责任固定在公司名号背后的那个真人身上。

abstract.en: A mask becomes an adverb: the word now describes how a person steps forward in his own body.
abstract.cn: 面具变成了副词：这个词现在描述一个人如何以自己的肉身站出来。

abstract.en: Personally is a small flag planted on a sentence to show that one particular speaker is standing behind it.
abstract.cn: personally 是插在句子上的一面小旗，表明有某一个具体的说话人站在它后面。

abstract.en: The distance between a rule and the person it hits is exactly the space this adverb measures.
abstract.cn: 规则与它所击中的人之间的距离，正是这个副词丈量的空间。

examples.en: The chef personally tasted every dish before service.
examples.cn: 上菜之前，主厨亲自尝了每一道菜。

examples.en: Personally, I think the plan is too risky.
examples.cn: 就我个人而言，我觉得这个计划风险太大。

examples.en: Please do not take this personally, but your report needs more evidence.
examples.cn: 请别把这话当成针对你，不过你的报告还需要更多证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼森呢哩」——破伞的人宁可自己淋雨，也要亲自把伞递到你手上；personally 就是亲自。

root: 拉丁语 persona（面具、角色）构成 personalis，再进入英语成为形容词 personal，加 -ly 得到 personally；核心始终是某一个具体的人。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb keeps the noun of person alive: it can mean the body that acts, the mind that judges, the target of an insult, or the name on a legal duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词始终活在「人」这个名词里：它可以指动手的身体、下判断的头脑、被冒犯的对象，也可以指法律责任上的那个名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching past an offered helper and lifting the box by itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把袖口挽起，越过别人伸来的手，自己把箱子搬起来。

branches.en: a manager handing out letters one by one
branches.cn: 经理一封一封把信递出去

branches.en: a raised hand before an opinion is given
branches.cn: 给出看法之前先举起一只手

branches.en: a remark that lands on the wrong target
branches.cn: 一句话落到了错的目标上

branches.en: a signature under a clause about damage
branches.cn: 损失条款下方的一个签名

branches.en: the same voice saying I did it and I think so
branches.cn: 同一个声音说「我做的」和「我认为」

intro.en: The adverb is a chain of three built pieces: a Latin noun, a Latin adjective ending and a native adverb ending.
intro.cn: 这个副词是三段构造成果串起来的：一个拉丁名词、一个拉丁形容词词尾，一个本族副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Only the noun and the adjective are Latin; the adverb itself was assembled inside English with a native ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了那个名词和形容词；副词本身是英语用本族词尾自行拼起来的。

definition_zh: 全体员工；人事部门；（军队或机构的）人员；某类专业人员
definition_en: the people who work for an organization, or the department that manages them; also the members of a force or of a particular group of workers
core_image: 一整面挂满名牌的墙，每块名牌后面都有一个正在上班的人
scene: 清晨的办公楼里，打卡机一声声响起，走廊尽头的人事办公室门口已经排起了队。The personnel files were moved to the third floor last week.
sceneCN: 这里 personnel 指「人事部门」（第 2 个义项：管理员工档案与招聘的部门）；句意为上周人事档案被搬到了三层。图中可辨识物件：打卡机、走廊、写着「人事」的门牌。

pos.zh: 全体员工；人事部门；人员

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 persona（面具、角色）而来，义为「人；个人」
由 person 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「个人的；私人的」
由 personal 加 -ity 构成，义为「个性；人格」
由 personal 加 -ly 构成，义为「亲自；就个人而言」

senses.title: All the people who work for an organization
senses.definition: the whole body of people employed by a company, school, or other organization, considered as one group
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于公司、学校或其他机构的全体人员，被当作一个整体来看
senses.example: The company doubled its personnel within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在一年之内把员工人数翻了一倍。
senses.why: The word entered English as the noun use of a French adjective meaning personal, so it named the persons attached to an organization before it named any office or list.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时，是法语中意为「个人的」那个形容词直接当名词用，所以它先指「挂靠在一个机构下的那些人」，而不是先指某个办公室或名册。

senses.title: The department that hires staff and keeps their records
senses.definition: the office in an organization that deals with hiring, records, and the terms of employment
senses.definitionCN: 机构中负责招聘、档案与雇佣条件的部门
senses.example: She works in personnel at the head office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在总部的人事部门工作。
senses.why: Because personnel already meant the people themselves, the office that counts and files those people took the same name by metonymy, the container named after what it contains.
senses.whyCN: 既然 personnel 已经指人本身，负责清点、归档这些人的办公室就借用了同一个名字，这是以「所管之物」代指「管理机构」的转喻。

senses.title: The members of an armed force, counted as a body
senses.definition: the members of a military force or unit, especially when they are counted or listed
senses.definitionCN: 军队或部队的成员，尤指被清点、列入名册时
senses.example: The wounded personnel were flown out at night.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤人员夜间被空运撤离。
senses.why: Military paperwork treats soldiers as entries on a roll, so personnel in this sense means the names on the list rather than any single soldier.
senses.whyCN: 军队的文书把士兵当成名册上的一条记录，所以这个义项里的 personnel 指名单上的那些人，而不指某一个士兵。

senses.title: People of one particular kind working in an operation
senses.definition: the people of a specified profession or role who are present in a place or taking part in an activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一行业或某一职责的人，出现在某个场所或参与某项行动
senses.example: Medical personnel arrived within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗人员在十分钟内赶到。
senses.why: The collective frame survives even when the group is defined by a profession, so personnel can attach to a type of worker rather than to a single employer.
senses.whyCN: 即使这群人是由职业来界定的，那个「集体」的框架依然保留，所以 personnel 可以挂在一类工作者身上，而不必依附于某一个雇主。

intro.en: Personnel is a French adjective that became a noun: it began as the personal and ended up meaning the persons.
intro.cn: personnel 本是法语里的一个形容词，后来转成名词：起点是「个人的」，终点是「那些人」。

items.en: Persona first meant a mask worn by an actor, then the role played, and finally the individual who plays it.
items.cn: persona 最初指演员戴的面具，接着指所扮演的角色，最后指扮演角色的那个人。

items.en: The adjective personalis was built on persona and meant belonging to a person.
items.cn: 形容词 personalis 由 persona 构成，意为「属于某个人的」。

items.en: Old French used personel for what belongs to one person, and this form reached English as personal.
items.cn: 古法语用 personel 表示「属于个人的」，这一形式进入英语后成为 personal。

items.en: French turned its adjective personnel into a noun for the staff of an office, and English borrowed that noun in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语把自己的形容词 personnel 转为名词，指一个机关的全班人员；英语在十九世纪初借来了这个名词。

items.en: English kept the French -el spelling, added the human-resources sense in the twentieth century, and still treats the word as a collective with no ordinary singular.
items.cn: 英语保留了法语 -el 的拼法，二十世纪又添上「人事部门」这一义项，并且至今把它当作集合名词，没有日常的单数形式。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin persona through French and English; the near-meaning group gathers words for the people who work somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语 persona 经法语到英语的线索排列；近义组收表示「在某处工作的人」的词。

entries.definition: A single human being, seen as an individual.
entries.definitionCN: 单个的人，作为一个个体来看。

entries.definition: Belonging to or concerning one particular person.
entries.definitionCN: 属于或关于某一个特定的人的。

entries.definition: The set of qualities that make someone who they are.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某人之为某人的那套性格特质。

entries.definition: To pretend to be another person, often to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 假装成另一个人，常带有欺骗目的。

entries.definition: The people who work for a particular organization, treated as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一机构工作的全体人员，作为整体看待。

entries.definition: All the people who are able to work in a country or company.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家或公司里所有能工作的人。

entries.definition: The people who are paid to work for an employer.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇于雇主、领取报酬工作的人。

entries.definition: A team of people working together, especially on a ship or aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 一起工作的一队人，尤指船或飞机上的全体人员。

normalIntro.en: The word is a French adjective sitting in a noun's chair, and its whole family runs back to the Latin mask.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是坐在名词位置上的法语形容词，而它的整个词族都要回到拉丁语的「面具」那里。

normal.en: Personnel is the noun use of a French adjective meaning personal, so it names persons rather than things.
normal.cn: personnel 是法语中意为「个人的」那个形容词当名词用，所以它指人而不指物。

normal.en: The ending -el is French; English personal uses -al, and that one letter is the main reason the two words are so easily confused.
normal.cn: 词尾 -el 来自法语；英语的 personal 用 -al，这一个字母的差别正是两词极易混淆的主因。

normal.en: As a collective noun it normally takes no plural, and one worker is a member of the personnel, not a personnel.
normal.cn: 作为集合名词，它通常不加复数；单独一个人要说成「人员中的一员」，而不能直接说成一个人。

normal.en: Personnel department shortened to personnel is a metonymy: the office is named after the people it manages.
normal.cn: 把「人事部门」缩成 personnel 是转喻：办公室被按它所管理的人来命名。

normal.en: In military reports personnel is the count on the roll, so losses are reported as personnel losses rather than as individual names.
normal.cn: 在军事报告里，personnel 就是名册上的数目，所以损失按「人员损失」统计，而不逐个列名字。

abstract.en: Think of a wall of name tags: the word never points at one tag, only at the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一整面名牌墙：这个词从不指向某一块名牌，只指向整面墙。

abstract.en: A French adjective walked into English and sat down as a noun; the stress still falls on the last syllable, as in French.
abstract.cn: 一个法语形容词走进英语，坐下当了名词；重音至今落在最后一个音节上，和法语一样。

abstract.en: One word covers both the people and the office that counts them, because paperwork always follows people.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指人，也指清点人的办公室，因为文书总是跟在人后面。

examples.en: All personnel must show their badges at the gate.
examples.cn: 所有员工都必须在大门口出示工牌。

examples.en: She was transferred to personnel after five years on the shop floor.
examples.cn: 在车间干了五年之后，她被调到了人事部门。

examples.en: Additional medical personnel were sent to the region.
examples.cn: 更多医疗人员被派往该地区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕搜人」——公司最怕搜不到合用的人，于是设了 personnel（人事部门）。

root: 来自拉丁语 persona（面具、角色、人）派生的形容词 personalis，经法语形容词 personnel 转为名词，指「属于某个机构的一群人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body of people attached to an organization; from that one collective sense grow the office that manages them, the roll of a military unit, and any named group of workers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是依附于某个机构的一群人；由这一个集合义长出管理他们的办公室、部队名册，以及任何被点名的一类专业工作者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of name tags, each one standing for a person who is on duty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面挂满名牌的墙，每块名牌后面都有一个在岗的人。

branches.en: a wall of name tags in a lobby
branches.cn: 大厅里一整面名牌墙

branches.en: a hospital corridor full of staff in different uniforms
branches.cn: 医院走廊里穿不同制服的各类人员

branches.en: a queue outside a glass door with files stacked behind it
branches.cn: 玻璃门前排着队，门后堆着一摞摞档案

branches.en: a list of names read aloud at roll call
branches.cn: 点名时被逐个念出的名单

branches.en: paperwork travelling from a barracks to an office
branches.cn: 文件从营房一路送到办公室

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin noun for a mask, its adjective, and a French ending that let the adjective become a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示面具的拉丁名词、它的形容词，以及一个让形容词变成名词的法语词尾共同构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: adjectival ending kept in the noun
items.meaningCN: 保留在名词里的形容词词尾

definition_zh: 观点；视角；透视法；洞察力；远景
definition_en: a particular way of seeing or thinking about something, the art of showing depth on a flat surface, or the ability to judge things in proportion
core_image: 站在一个固定的位置透过窗框看出去：位置一换，看到的东西就重排。
scene: 在农夫眼里，这场旱灾是灾难；在水库管理者眼里，却是喘息之机。From the perspective of a farmer, the drought is a disaster; from the reservoir's, it is a reprieve.
sceneCN: 这里 perspective 是「看问题的角度」（第 1 个义项：视角、观点）；句意：从农民的角度看，这场干旱是灾难；从水库的角度看，却是喘息之机。场景要点：干裂的田、下降的水位标尺；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: a particular way of looking at or thinking about something, shaped by where you stand
senses.definitionCN: 由于所处位置而形成的看或思考某事的特定方式
senses.example: The novel tells the same event from three perspectives.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说从三个视角讲述同一件事。
senses.why: Latin perspicere meant 'to look through'. Perspective is the view you get from one position, as if looking through a particular opening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perspicere 意为“看穿、看透”。perspective 就是从某一个位置透过特定开口所得到的视野。

senses.title: The ability to judge proportion
senses.titleCN: 分寸感：知道什么更重要
senses.definition: the ability to see how important things really are in relation to each other
senses.definitionCN: 看出事物之间真实轻重关系的能力
senses.example: Losing one game gave the team a sense of perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉一场比赛反而让球队有了分寸感。
senses.why: Depth in a drawing comes from things being the right size relative to distance. Judging importance is the same skill applied to life.
senses.whyCN: 画面中的纵深，来自物体相对于距离的正确大小。判断重要性，是把同一种本事用在生活上。

senses.title: Art: the geometry of depth
senses.titleCN: 透视法：让平面显出纵深
senses.definition: the technique of representing three-dimensional space and depth on a flat surface
senses.definitionCN: 在平面上表现三维空间与纵深的技法
senses.example: The fresco uses linear perspective to draw the eye down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画用线性透视把视线引向走廊深处。
senses.why: Renaissance painters formalized the idea that parallel lines converge to a vanishing point. Seeing 'through' the canvas is the literal source.
senses.whyCN: 文艺复兴画家把“平行线汇聚于消失点”形式化。透过画布“看进去”，正是这个词的字面来源。

senses.title: A distant view
senses.definition: a view, especially a wide or distant one, seen from a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 从某一地点看到的景色，尤指开阔或辽远的
senses.example: The ridge offers a perspective of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊上能看到整个山谷的远景。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense in English: what is seen from here, extending away from the viewer.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最古老的物理义：从这里看出去、向远处铺开的东西。

senses.title: A considered opinion on a matter
senses.definition: a considered attitude or evaluation of a subject, often one among several
senses.definitionCN: 对某主题经过思考的态度或评价，常为多种之一
senses.example: We need the perspective of someone outside the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要一位行业外人士的看法。
senses.why: The visual metaphor becomes argumentative: a standpoint is a place you stand, and what you see from there is your opinion.
senses.whyCN: 视觉比喻变成论辩性的：立场就是你站的地方，从那里看到的东西就是你的观点。

senses.title: Psychology: taking another's viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 换位思考：站到别人的位置
senses.definition: in psychology, the capacity to understand another person's point of view
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中理解他人视角的能力
senses.example: Perspective-taking improves negotiation outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 换位思考能改善谈判结果。
senses.why: The word is used literally here: you imagine standing where the other stands, and the scene rearranges itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里用的是字面义：你想象站到对方所站的位置，整个场景就重新排列了。

senses.title: Proportion restored: in perspective
senses.titleCN: 比例复原：把事放回它的尺寸
senses.definition: in the phrase in perspective, shown at its true relative size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in perspective，表示按真实的相对大小或重要性来看
senses.example: The loss looks small when seen in perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 从整体比例看，这点损失显得很小。
senses.why: In a correct drawing, near things are large and far things small. Seeing something 'in perspective' is seeing it at the size its distance deserves.
senses.whyCN: 在正确的画里，近的大、远的小。把某事“in perspective”看，就是按它的距离应得的大小去看。

senses.title: Geometry: projection from a viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 投影法：从视点投出去的几何
senses.definition: in geometry, the system that projects a scene onto a plane from a chosen point
senses.definitionCN: 几何中从选定视点把场景投射到平面上的体系
senses.example: Perspective projection distorts parallel lines, unlike orthographic projection.
senses.exampleCN: 与正交投影不同，透视投影会使平行线产生畸变。
senses.why: The artistic technique becomes a mathematical one: a chosen eye point and a plane, with straight lines from one to the other.
senses.whyCN: 艺术技法变成了数学体系：一个选定的眼点、一个平面，以及从一点到另一点的直线。

intro.en: Perspective is Latin perspicere 'to look through' turned into a noun. English first used it for the science of sight, then for the painter's technique, and only later for a mental point of view.
intro.cn: perspective 是拉丁语 perspicere“看穿”名词化的结果。英语先用它指视觉的科学，再指画家的技法，最后才指心里的观点。

items.en: Specere meant 'to look, see'. It is the root behind spectacle, inspect, respect, and perspective.
items.cn: specere 意为“看、看见”。它是 spectacle、inspect、respect、perspective 的词根。

items.en: Perspicere was per- 'through' + specere 'look': 'to see through, look at closely, perceive clearly'.
items.cn: perspicere 是 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”：“看透、仔细看、清楚感知”。

items.en: Perspectiva was the medieval Latin term for the science of optics, literally 'the things of seeing through'.
items.cn: perspectiva 是中古拉丁语对光学的称呼，字面是“看穿的诸事”。

items.en: English takes perspective in the 14th century as the name of the optical science. It is a learned term before it is an everyday one.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 perspective，作为光学学科的名称。它先是学术用语，后才进入日常。

items.en: The artistic sense, the technique of showing depth on a flat surface, is recorded by the 1590s. The scientific name becomes a painter's tool.
items.cn: 艺术义（在平面上表现纵深的技法）于 16 世纪 90 年代见于记录。学科名称变成了画家的工具。

items.en: The sense 'a view from a place' is recorded by the 1660s; the figurative 'mental point of view' by 1762. The metaphor of standing somewhere and looking is fully in place.
items.cn: “从某处看到的景色”义于 17 世纪 60 年代见于记录；比喻性的“心理观点”义于 1762 年。站在某处张望的比喻至此完全成形。

note.en: The first group shares the specere 'look' root; the second collects words for a way of seeing or judging.
note.cn: 第一组共享 specere“看”词根；第二组收“看事物的方式”类词。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things. It comes from the same perspicere but describes a person, not a viewpoint.
entries.definitionCN: 观察敏锐、理解快的。它同出 perspicere，但描述人，而不是视角。

entries.definition: having a ready insight into things; mentally sharp. A formal adjective from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 对事物有敏锐洞察力的；心智锐利的。同出那个拉丁动词的正式形容词。

entries.definition: a possibility of a future event, or a view ahead. Pro- 'forward' + specere 'look'; the direction is forward, not through.
entries.definitionCN: 未来事件的可能性，或前方的景色。pro-“向前”+ specere“看”；方向是向前，不是穿透。

entries.definition: relating to perspective or to a point of view
entries.definitionCN: 与透视或视角有关的（由 perspective 派生）

entries.definition: a person's opinion or way of thinking. It is the everyday equivalent of perspective and lacks the art and depth senses.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的意见或思考方式。它是 perspective 的日常对应词，没有艺术与纵深的义项。

entries.definition: a position from which a subject is considered, often in debate. It keeps the physical 'standing place' image openly.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑某主题时所处的立场，常用于论辩。它明着保留“站立之处”的意象。

entries.definition: a way of approaching a subject, especially one chosen to make it interesting. It is more informal and tactical.
entries.definitionCN: 切入某主题的方式，尤指为使它有趣而选择的。它更口语、更具策略性。

entries.definition: a person's attitude to life, or a forecast. It is broader and often about mood rather than analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对生活的态度，或前景预测。它更宽，常关于情绪而非分析。

entries.definition: a position giving a good view. It is the literal place from which a perspective is obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 能获得良好视野的位置。它就是取得某种 perspective 的字面地点。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin per- 'through' + specere 'look', giving perspicere 'see through'. Family words perspective, perspectival, perspectivism; relatives prospect, inspect, respect, spectacle.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”，合成 perspicere“看透”。词族为 perspective、perspectival、perspectivism；亲属词 prospect、inspect、respect、spectacle。

normal.en: Spectare is 'look': perspective is looking through a particular opening.
normal.cn: spectare 是“看”：perspective 就是透过某个特定开口去看。

normal.en: Prospect looks forward, perspective looks through; same verb, different prefix.
normal.cn: prospect 向前看，perspective 穿透看；同一动词，不同前缀。

normal.en: Linear perspective was a Renaissance rule: parallels meet at a vanishing point.
normal.cn: 线性透视是文艺复兴的规则：平行线在消失点相交。

normal.en: In perspective means at the size the distance deserves.
normal.cn: in perspective 就是按距离应得的大小来看。

normal.en: Perspective-taking is imagination used as a measuring instrument.
normal.cn: 换位思考，是把想象力当量尺来用。

abstract.en: Perspective is not a better view; it is a different place to stand.
abstract.cn: 视角不是更好的视野，而是另一个站立之处。

abstract.en: Depth exists only because some things are allowed to be small.
abstract.cn: 纵深之所以存在，只因有些东西被允许变小。

abstract.en: The ability to change perspective is the cheapest form of mercy.
abstract.cn: 能换一个视角，是最廉价的慈悲。

examples.en: Try to see the decision from the perspective of a new employee.
examples.cn: 试着从新员工的角度看这个决定。

examples.en: The bad quarter should be put into perspective against ten years of growth.
examples.cn: 这个糟糕的季度应当放到十年增长的比例中来看。

examples.en: Brunelleschi's experiment demonstrated linear perspective in painting.
examples.cn: 布鲁内莱斯基的实验展示了绘画中的线性透视。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破视野·派克提夫”——派克提着窗框站定，换个位置就换一片视野 → perspective 视角、透视

root: 源自拉丁语 perspicere“看穿、看清”，由 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”构成；中世纪拉丁语 perspectiva 是“光学”，英语 14 世纪借入，16 世纪 90 年代转指绘画透视，1660 年代有“景色”义，1762 年才有比喻性的“观点”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of perspective, all one geometry: a viewpoint, a plane, and the lines that connect them.
sensesIntro.cn: perspective 的八个义项是同一个几何关系：一个视点、一个平面，以及连接二者的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye at a fixed point looking through a frame at a scene that recedes to a vanishing point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只眼固定在一点，透过窗框看出去，景物向消失点退去。

branches.en: MIND: where you stand and what you conclude — the viewpoint and the opinion it produces.
branches.cn: 心智：站在哪里与得出什么——视角以及由它产生的看法。

branches.en: EMPATHY: moving your own eye to another point, the viewpoint taken as an act.
branches.cn: 共情：把自己的眼移到另一点，视角由“位置”变成“动作”。

branches.en: PROPORTION: judging importance is drawing depth, and in perspective restores true size.
branches.cn: 比例：判断重要性就是画纵深，而 in perspective 是恢复真实大小。

branches.en: TECHNIQUE: the painter's vanishing point and the geometer's projection are one system, formalized.
branches.cn: 技法：画家的消失点与几何学家的投影，是同一个体系的形式化。

branches.en: LANDSCAPE: the oldest physical sense, what lies spread out in front of the eye.
branches.cn: 景物：最古老的物理义，铺展在眼前的那一片。

intro.en: Perspective's family is built on Latin specere 'to look'. Suffixes mark the adjective and the doctrine; compounds name the techniques and the mental acts.
intro.cn: perspective 的词族建立在拉丁语 specere“看”上。后缀标记形容词与学说；复合词则命名技法与心理活动。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are specere 'look', perspicere 'see through', and perspectiva, the medieval Latin name for optics.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是 specere“看”、perspicere“看透”与 perspectiva——中世纪拉丁语对光学的称呼。

items.meaning: a viewpoint, or the art of showing depth
items.meaningCN: 视角；表现纵深的技法（来自拉丁语 perspectiva）
items.example: The two reports offer opposite perspectives.
items.exampleCN: 两份报告提供了相反的视角。

items.meaning: relating to a perspective or viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 与透视或视角有关的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The drawing has a strong perspectival structure.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画有很强的透视结构。

items.meaning: the view that knowledge is always from some perspective
items.meaningCN: 认为知识总是出自某种视角的主张（-ism 构成主义名词）
items.example: Nietzsche's perspectivism denies a view from nowhere.
items.exampleCN: 尼采的视角主义否认存在“无处之见”。

items.meaning: the act of imagining another person's viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 想象他人视角的行为（心理学用语）
items.exampleCN: 换位思考能减少团队冲突。

items.meaning: depth shown by lines converging on a vanishing point
items.meaningCN: 用线条汇聚于消失点来表现纵深（艺术术语）
items.example: The street is drawn in strict linear perspective.
items.exampleCN: 这条街用严格的线性透视画出。

items.meaning: depth shown by making distant things hazier and bluer
items.meaningCN: 通过使远处景物更朦胧、更偏蓝来表现纵深
items.example: The mountains fade by aerial perspective.
items.exampleCN: 群山因空气透视而渐淡。

items.meaning: seen at its true relative size or importance
items.meaningCN: 按真实的相对大小或重要性来看
items.example: The problem looks manageable in perspective.
items.exampleCN: 放到整体里看，问题并不难办。

items.meaning: to compare something so that its real importance becomes clear
items.meaningCN: 通过比较使某事的真实重要性显现
items.example: The figures put the loss into perspective.
items.exampleCN: 这些数字让损失的大小变得清楚。

items.meaning: a projection from a viewpoint that makes far things smaller
items.meaningCN: 从视点投射、使远处物体变小的投影法
items.example: Games use perspective projection to create depth.
items.exampleCN: 游戏用透视投影制造纵深。

items.meaning: a drawing made according to the rules of depth
items.example: The class began with perspective drawing.

definition_zh: 说服；劝使（某人做某事）；打动并争取过来
definition_en: to cause someone to accept a belief or to take an action by giving reasons or by winning them over
core_image: 一间小屋里，散乱的证词被摆成一条直线，听者沿着线走到说话人站的结论处
scene: 答辩室里，年轻讲师把一页图表推到委员面前，零散的数据连成一条能读下去的线。A single clear chart helped the young lecturer persuade the skeptical committee to fund the project.
sceneCN: 这里 persuade 指「用理由使人接受某个结论」（第 1 个义项：以论证令听者信服）；句意为一张清晰的图表让这位年轻讲师说服了原本怀疑的委员会为该项目拨款。可辨识物件：投影幕、图表、水杯、委员的名牌；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.phrase: persuade somebody out of a decision
collocations.zh: 劝某人改掉已定的主意

derivatives.zh: 说服；说服力；信念
有说服力的
有说服力地
说服力
劝说者
容易被说服的

senses.title: Make someone accept a conclusion
senses.titleCN: 以论证使人接受某个结论
senses.definition: to cause a person to believe that something is true by presenting reasons
senses.definitionCN: 通过摆出理由，使某人相信某事为真
senses.example: The report persuaded the board that the old warehouse could be converted.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告使董事会相信，那座旧仓库可以改造。
senses.why: the oldest layer of the word is advice: per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere 'to advise' yields 'advise until the point is carried'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是「进言」：per-「彻底」加 suadere「劝告」，合起来就是「劝到对方接受为止」。

senses.title: Urge someone to act
senses.definition: to talk someone into doing something they might not otherwise do
senses.definitionCN: 劝得某人去做他本不一定会做的事
senses.example: She persuaded her brother to take the later train.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服弟弟改乘晚一班火车。
senses.why: once the listener accepts the reasons, the next step is to move: advice about an act becomes advice to perform it.
senses.whyCN: 听者接受理由之后，下一步就是行动：关于「该怎么做」的进言，自然变成「去做」的劝使。

senses.title: Succeed where others failed
senses.titleCN: 把原本不肯的一方争取过来
senses.definition: to win over someone who has resisted argument, so that the attempt succeeds
senses.definitionCN: 把一直抗拒说理的一方争取过来，使劝说真正成功
senses.example: After two hours of argument he finally persuaded the holdouts.
senses.exampleCN: 争辩了两个小时，他终于说服了那几个坚持不让步的人。
senses.why: modern English treats persuade as a success verb: to say you persuaded someone is to say the person yielded.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把 persuade 当作「结果动词」：说「说服了某人」，就等于说对方已经让步。

senses.title: Win someone over by feeling
senses.titleCN: 靠情感打动而争取过来
senses.definition: to gain a person's agreement through warmth, charm or emotional appeal rather than proof
senses.definitionCN: 不靠证明，而以温情、魅力或情感打动来取得对方同意
senses.example: The singer's account persuaded even the reporters who had come to sneer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位歌手的讲述甚至打动了本来打算嘲弄她的记者。
senses.why: suadere is generally thought to be tied to suavis 'sweet', so the word has always carried a hint of pleasantness as well as argument.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为 suadere 与 suavis「甜的」相关，因此这个词除了论理，一直带着一点「可亲、顺耳」的意味。

senses.title: Come to believe after hearing
senses.titleCN: 被动义：听过之后转而相信
senses.definition: to become convinced of something oneself, especially in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 自己听过之后转为相信，多见于被动结构
senses.example: I was persuaded by the data, not by the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 让我信服的是数据，那番演讲并没有说服我。
senses.why: when the verb is passive, the listener moves to the side of the speaker, and the action is viewed from the receiving end.
senses.whyCN: 用于被动时，听者移到说话人这一边，动作便从「接受的一方」来看。

senses.title: Advise or urge strongly
senses.definition: to urge or advise a course of action forcefully, without implying that the advice was taken
senses.definitionCN: 强烈敦促或建议某种做法，不含「已被采纳」之意
senses.example: The old manuals persuade the reader to test each joint twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这些旧手册力劝读者把每个接缝都测两遍。
senses.why: seventeenth-century English used persuade where modern English would say urge; the success reading only became fixed later.
senses.whyCN: 十七世纪的英语在今天的 urge 之处用 persuade；「成功」这层读法是后来才固定的。

senses.title: Talk oneself into believing
senses.definition: to bring oneself to accept something uncomfortable or doubtful
senses.definitionCN: 让自己接受某种令人不安或未必可靠的事
senses.example: He persuaded himself that the delay was harmless.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服自己相信这次延误并无妨碍。
senses.why: the mind can play both roles, speaker and listener, so the verb turns reflexive and describes inner bargaining.
senses.whyCN: 头脑可以同时扮演说话人与听者，于是这个动词转为自反，描述内心里的讨价还价。

senses.title: Swing a group as a whole
senses.definition: to change the decision of a body or assembly rather than a single person
senses.definitionCN: 使一个机构或集会整体改变决定，而非只改变一个人
senses.example: The petition persuaded the council to reopen the footpath.
senses.exampleCN: 请愿书使议会重新开放那条步道。
senses.why: a council votes as one voice, so persuading it means shifting the majority inside it.
senses.whyCN: 议会按一个声音投票，因此说服议会，实际上就是让其中的多数改向。

senses.title: Win people to a cause
senses.titleCN: 使人归附某种信念或事业
senses.definition: to convert people to a faith, party or cause one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐个把人争取到某种信仰、党派或事业这一边
senses.example: Missionaries persuaded villagers one household at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 传教士一家一家地把村民争取过来。
senses.why: the same winning-over gesture, repeated person by person, becomes the language of conversion and recruitment.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「争取过来」的动作，一个人一个人地重复，就成了皈依与招纳的说法。

intro.en: Persuade entered English from Latin persuadere 'to urge thoroughly, prevail upon', built on per- 'thoroughly' and suadere 'to advise, urge'. Suadere is generally thought to be related to suavis 'sweet'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: persuade 从拉丁 persuadere「劝到底、争取过来」进入英语，由 per-「彻底」与 suadere「劝告、敦促」构成。一般认为 suadere 与 suavis「甜的」相关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Suadere meant 'to advise, recommend, urge'. The connection with suavis 'sweet, pleasant' is generally thought to be genuine, but the similarity alone does not prove it, and any deeper Indo-European shape for it exists only as a reconstructed form.
items.cn: suadere 意为「劝告、推荐、敦促」。它与 suavis「甜的、可亲的」的联系一般认为是真实的，但仅凭音形相近不足以证明；为它构拟的更早印欧形式只以重构形式存在。

items.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere produced persuadere, 'to advise thoroughly, to prevail upon, to convince'. The prefix turns a piece of advice into an action carried through.
items.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere 构成 persuadere，意为「劝到底、争取过来、使信服」。这个前缀把一句劝告变成一个做到底的动作。

items.en: The verb appears in English in the late fourteenth century, either taken straight from Latin or through Middle French persuader.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪晚期出现于英语，或直接取自拉丁语，或经中古法语 persuader 传入。

items.en: Early modern English still used the word for plain urging, where a modern writer would choose urge or advise; no success was implied.
items.cn: 早期现代英语仍用它表示单纯的「力劝」，今天的写作者会改用 urge 或 advise；当时并不含成功之意。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the success reading had settled in, and the passive 'be persuaded' became the ordinary way to report a change of mind.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，「劝说成功」的读法已经固定，被动式「被说服」成为报告改变想法的常说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation and deeper origin): the earliest dated example varies between dictionaries, and every pre-Latin form offered for suadere is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证与更深来源）：各家词典给出的最早年代并不一致；凡为 suadere 提出的拉丁语之前形式，都是重构形式，而非有书证的词。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look or sound close to persuade, one of which is not related at the root at all; group two gathers verbs that also move a listener but with a different lever.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，其中一个在词根上与本词毫无关系；第二组收同样能推动听者、但所用杠杆不同的动词。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus suadere, so it means to advise someone away from an action, the mirror image of persuade.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「离开」加 suadere，意为劝人不要做某事，正是 persuade 的镜像。

entries.definition: From Old French assouagier, from a Latin stem built on suavis 'sweet': to soften or soothe pain, sharing the sweet root but not the advising root.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语 assouagier，出自以 suavis「甜的」为基的拉丁词干：减轻、抚慰痛苦；与「甜」同根，却不走「劝告」这一支。

entries.tag: rare noun of the same verb
entries.definition: The formal noun from Latin suasio 'a advising', now mostly confined to the phrase moral suasion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 suasio「劝告」的正式名词，如今基本只用于「道义劝告」这一说法。

entries.definition: From Latin prosequi 'follow after', built on sequi 'to follow'; it looks close to persuade but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 prosequi「跟随」，由 sequi「跟随」构成；字形与 persuade 相近，词根却毫无关系。

entries.definition: To bring someone to accept a fact as true; the emphasis is on belief rather than on action.
entries.definitionCN: 使人接受某事实为真；侧重「相信」，而非「行动」。

entries.definition: To obtain something by gentle, patient urging; there is no argument, only smooth persistence.
entries.definitionCN: 靠温和耐心的劝哄取得某物；不讲道理，只靠柔和的坚持。

entries.definition: To influence a crowd or a decision, often through emotion; it is weaker on proof than persuade.
entries.definitionCN: 影响人群或决定，常借情感；在「论证」上比 persuade 弱。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for getting someone to agree by persistent asking, common in letters and speeches.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的「恳请」说法，靠一再请求使人同意，多见于书信与演说。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere 'advise': advice carried all the way through.
normal.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere「劝告」：把劝告做到底。

normal.en: The family runs persuade, persuasion, persuasive, persuasively, persuasiveness, persuader.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 persuade、persuasion、persuasive、persuasively、persuasiveness、persuader。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the two objects: persuade somebody to act, persuade somebody of a fact.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出两类宾语：劝人去做、使人相信某事实。

normal.en: The reverse verb is dissuade, built with the prefix that means apart.
normal.cn: 反向的动词是 dissuade，由表示「离开」的前缀构成。

normal.en: Passive reports are common: the committee was persuaded, the jury was persuaded.
normal.cn: 被动说法很常见：委员会被说服、陪审团被说服。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door that opens only after every key has been tried in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门，只有按顺序试过每一把钥匙才会开。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that tips only when a pebble is added to one side.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，只有在一侧再加一粒小石子时才倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a listener walking along a rope the speaker has laid out.
abstract.cn: 想象听者沿着说话人铺好的绳子往前走。

examples.en: Nothing could persuade the old farmer to sell the orchard.
examples.cn: 什么也无法说服那位老农卖掉果园。

examples.en: The teacher persuaded the class that the experiment was worth repeating.
examples.cn: 老师让全班相信这个实验值得重做一遍。

examples.en: He was persuaded only after he had read the original letters.
examples.cn: 他读过原始信件之后才被说服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「per（彻底）+ suade（劝）」——一直劝到对方彻底点头 → 说服

root: 拉丁 persuadere「劝到底、争取过来」= per-（彻底）+ suadere「劝告、敦促」；suadere 与 suavis「甜的」的联系一般认为是同源，更深印欧形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: reasons are laid out, the listener is urged, belief settles, and belief turns into action or into a whole group changing course.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：先摆出理由，再向听者进言，信念落定，最后信念转为行动，或转为整群人改向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of reasons laid out on a table, along which a doubtful listener walks to the speaker's side.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上铺开一条理由的线，心存怀疑的听者沿着它走到说话人一边。

branches.en: ADVICE COMPLETED: the oldest layer is urging and advising, carried through to the end.
branches.cn: 把劝告做到底：最古老的一层是敦促与进言，一直做到终点。

branches.en: ACTION AND ASSEMBLY: a single listener is moved to act, then a whole council is moved to change course.
branches.cn: 行动与全体：先推动一个听者去做，再推动整个议会改向。

branches.en: BELIEF SURRENDERED: the resisting mind yields, and the passive form reports the change from the receiving side.
branches.cn: 信念让步：抗拒的一方松手，被动式则从接受方报告这一变化。

branches.en: SWEET PRESSURE: charm and warmth do the work that proof cannot do.
branches.cn: 甜的推力：证明做不到的事，由魅力与温情做到。

branches.en: INNER AND OUTER CONVERSION: the same voice persuades oneself, or persuades a household at a time.
branches.cn: 向内向外的皈依：同一个声音，可以劝服自己，也可以一家一家地劝服。

intro.en: Persuade is a Latin verb whose prefix and root still build English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: persuade 是一个拉丁动词，其前缀与词根至今仍在构成英语词，因此整个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin suadere gives persuade, dissuade, suasion and assuage; the prefix per- adds the sense of doing something thoroughly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 suadere 衍生 persuade、dissuade、suasion 与 assuage；前缀 per- 增添「彻底」之意。

items.example: The prefix marks the advice as carried through to success.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把关切标记为一直做到成功。

items.example: The root contributes the whole idea of advising.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贡献了「劝告」的全部意思。
那张图表说服了委员会。

items.example: A neighbour dissuaded him from signing.
items.exampleCN: 一位邻居劝他不要签字。

items.meaning: the act or result of persuading
items.example: The argument needed no further persuasion.
items.exampleCN: 这个论点无需再作说服。

items.example: She wrote a persuasive letter to the editor.
items.exampleCN: 她给编辑写了一封有说服力的信。

items.example: He argued persuasively for a second trial.
items.exampleCN: 他有力地为再次试验辩护。

items.example: The persuasiveness of the data surprised the panel.
items.exampleCN: 数据之有说服力让评审组意外。

items.example: The campaign relied on moral suasion.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动依靠道义劝告。

definition_zh: 汽油；（作定语）汽油的；汽油蓝
definition_en: a light liquid fuel refined from petroleum and burned in the engines of cars, sold in Britain under this name rather than as gasoline
core_image: 油枪插进油箱，透明液体带着刺鼻气味灌进去，车子随即又能跑起来
scene: 冬天的清晨，加油站前排着长队，车窗上全是白雾。By the time the tank was full of petrol, the driver's hands had gone numb.
sceneCN: 这里是「汽油」（第 1 个义项：机动车用的轻质燃料）；句意为加满汽油的时候，司机的手已经冻得发麻。图中可辨识物件：加油枪、结霜的车窗、跳动的油表。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干构成的源词，指地下开采的原油，是 petrol 的上位概念
由 petrol 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「汽油的；含汽油的」
由希腊词根 petro-（岩石）与 chemical 复合，指石油化工产品

senses.title: Motor fuel refined from petroleum
senses.definition: a light, flammable liquid made from petroleum and used as fuel in the engines of cars and other vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 由石油炼制的轻质易燃液体，用作汽车等内燃机的燃料
senses.example: The car ran out of petrol halfway up the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 车在上坡途中没油了。
senses.why: British drivers name the fluid itself, and the word began as a shortening of petroleum spirit, the thin fraction that boils off crude oil first and burns most easily in an engine.
senses.whyCN: 英国人说这个词时指的是那种液体本身；它最初是 petroleum spirit（石油精）的缩略，也就是原油蒸馏时最先沸腾、在发动机里最容易燃烧的轻馏分，所以词义天然落在「车用轻质燃料」上。

senses.title: Used before a noun for anything running on this fuel
senses.definition: placed before another noun to describe an engine, vehicle or place that uses or supplies this fuel
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，说明某发动机、车辆或场所使用或供应这种燃料
senses.example: He pulled into a petrol station just before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜前他把车开进了一个加油站。
senses.why: Because everyday British speech has no verb of its own for refuelling, the fuel word is simply set in front of nouns such as engine, tank and station, where it labels whatever runs on it.
senses.whyCN: 日常英式表达里没有专门表示「加油」的动词形式，于是这个燃料词被直接放在 engine、tank、station 这类名词前面，给一切靠它运转的东西贴标签，定语用法就是这样固定下来的。

senses.title: A deep blue-green shade
senses.definition: a dark blue-green colour named after the rainbow film that fuel leaves on water
senses.definitionCN: 一种深蓝绿色调，得名于燃料在水面留下的彩虹色油膜
senses.example: The kitchen wall was painted petrol blue.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的墙刷成了汽油蓝。
senses.why: Thin oil on a wet road shows a shifting blue-green sheen, and decorators borrowed the fuel's name for that exact shade, so the colour sense is the same liquid seen in a different light.
senses.whyCN: 湿路面上的一层薄油会泛出流动的蓝绿色光泽，室内设计师便借燃料之名来称呼这种具体的色调；所以颜色义项仍是同一种液体，只是换了一种光线去看。

intro.en: Petrol is a nineteenth-century shortening of petroleum spirit, and its family goes back through French to a medieval Latin name meaning rock oil.
intro.cn: petrol 是十九世纪对 petroleum spirit（石油精）的缩略，其词族经法语上溯到中世纪拉丁语中意为「岩石油」的名称。

items.en: Greek petra meant rock or stone, and it supplied the first half of the later name for oil that seeps out of stone.
items.cn: 希腊语 petra 意为岩石、石头，为后来「从石头里渗出的油」这一名称提供了前半部分。

items.en: Latin oleum meant oil, and the two elements were later joined to describe mineral oil rather than plant oil.
items.cn: 拉丁语 oleum 意为油；后来两个成分被拼在一起，用来指矿物油而不是植物油。

items.en: Medieval Latin petroleum, literally rock oil, named the oily substance that seeped from rock and was once sold as medicine.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 petroleum 字面即「岩石油」，指从岩石中渗出的油状物，曾作为药物出售。

items.en: French pétrole named the refined oil, while English pharmacists spoke of petroleum spirit for the light, volatile part of it.
items.cn: 法语 pétrole 指炼出的油，英语药剂师则用 petroleum spirit 称呼其中轻而易挥发的那一部分。

items.en: English cut petroleum spirit down to petrol in the late nineteenth century, and the short form became the everyday British word for motor fuel.
items.cn: 十九世纪后期英语把 petroleum spirit 截短为 petrol，这个短形式后来成为英式英语里指车用燃料的日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same rock-and-oil stem; the near-meaning group gathers other fuels sold at the same pump.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「岩石加油」词干上的词；近义组收在同一个加油机上出售的其他燃料。

entries.definition: The crude oil from which petrol is refined; the longer source word.
entries.definitionCN: 汽油由它炼制而来的原油，也是 petrol 的长形式源词。

entries.definition: A chemical obtained from petroleum or natural gas.
entries.definitionCN: 从石油或天然气中提取的化学品。

entries.definition: The scientific study of rocks, built on the same Greek word for rock.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石的科学，建立在同一个表示「岩石」的希腊词上。

entries.definition: Containing or yielding petroleum, as certain rock layers do.
entries.definitionCN: 含石油或产石油的，如某些岩层。

entries.definition: The American word for the same motor fuel.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语里指同一种车用燃料的词。

entries.definition: A heavier fuel burned in a different kind of engine.
entries.definitionCN: 一种更重的燃料，用于另一种发动机。

entries.definition: Any material burned or consumed to produce heat or power.
entries.definitionCN: 任何燃烧或消耗以产生热或动力的材料。

entries.definition: A thin oil used in lamps and jet engines, lighter than diesel.
entries.definitionCN: 用于灯和喷气发动机的轻质油，比柴油更轻。

normalIntro.en: Petrol is a clipped piece of a much older compound, so its family keeps returning to rock, oil and the lightest part of both.
normalIntro.cn: petrol 是从一个古老得多的复合词里截下来的，所以它的同族词总是回到岩石、油以及两者中最轻的那一部分。

normal.en: Petrol is a clipped form of petroleum spirit, so the word still carries the idea of the lightest part of crude oil.
normal.cn: petrol 是 petroleum spirit 的截短形式，所以这个词始终带着「原油中最轻那部分」的意思。

normal.en: The same stem appears in petroleum, petrochemical and petrology, all tied to rock and the oil drawn from it.
normal.cn: 同一词干出现在 petroleum、petrochemical、petrology 里，都与岩石以及从岩石中取得的油有关。

normal.en: British petrol and American gasoline name the same pump fuel, so a naming habit rather than a chemical difference separates them.
normal.cn: 英式 petrol 与美式 gasoline 指同一种加油站的燃料，分开它们的只是命名习惯，而不是化学成分。

normal.en: Petrol station, petrol tank and petrol engine show the word behaving like a fixed label in front of nouns.
normal.cn: petrol station、petrol tank、petrol engine 表明这个词常像固定标签一样放在名词前。

normal.en: Petrol blue is not a joke: the word for the fuel also names the blue-green film it leaves on water.
normal.cn: petrol blue 不是玩笑：这个燃料词也用来命名它在水面留下的蓝绿色油膜。

abstract.en: Picture the clear liquid sliding down the filler neck: the word names the moment a car becomes able to move again.
abstract.cn: 想象透明液体顺着加油口流下去：这个词命名的正是汽车重新能跑起来的那一刻。

abstract.en: A fuel thin enough to explode in a cylinder is also thin enough to shimmer on a puddle, which is why one word covers both.
abstract.cn: 薄到能在气缸里爆燃的燃料，也薄到能在水洼上泛光，于是一个词同时覆盖了这两件事。

abstract.en: Every litre of petrol is ancient sunlight stored underground and released in a few minutes of driving.
abstract.cn: 每一升汽油都是储存在地下的远古阳光，在几分钟的驾驶里被释放出来。

examples.en: The car ran out of petrol halfway up the hill.
examples.cn: 车在上坡途中没油了。

examples.en: Petrol prices rose again before the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期前汽油价格又涨了。

examples.en: He pulled into a petrol station just before midnight.
examples.cn: 午夜前他把车开进了一个加油站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼漏」——油箱一颠，油泼出来又漏下去；petrol 是汽油。

root: 拉丁语 petra（岩石，源自希腊语）加 oleum（油）构成中世纪拉丁语 petroleum，经法语进入英语；十九世纪截短为 petrol，专指原油炼出的轻质车用燃料。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the light fuel burned in a car engine; from it come the attributive label for petrol-driven things and the colour named after an oil film.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是汽车发动机里燃烧的轻质燃料；由此分出去定语用法（汽油驱动的）与以油膜命名的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nozzle clicking shut as clear fuel rises inside the tank.
core.cn: 核心意象：透明燃料在油箱里升高，加油枪咔哒一声跳停。

branches.en: a pump nozzle clicking off as the tank fills
branches.cn: 加油枪在油箱加满时咔哒一声跳停

branches.en: a needle on the dashboard dropping toward empty
branches.cn: 仪表盘上的指针滑向空位

branches.en: a station lit up at midnight beside a dark road
branches.cn: 深夜公路旁亮着灯的加油站

branches.en: a blue-green sheen spreading over a rain puddle
branches.cn: 蓝绿色光泽在雨后的水洼上散开

branches.en: the same thin liquid, once burned and once reflected
branches.cn: 同一种轻质液体，一面被烧掉，一面被映照

intro.en: The word is a compound of a Greek rock word and a Latin oil word, later clipped and pressed into service as the British name for motor fuel.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语的「岩石」与拉丁语的「油」复合而成，后来被截短，用作英式英语里车用燃料的名称。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 化学名称中表示油或醇的后缀

senses.example: The first phase of the trial focuses on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 试验的第一阶段重点关注安全性。
senses.why: The word starts from the moon: its endless cycle is cut into named segments. Any long human process is cut the same way, so one segment is a phase.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起于月亮：月亮无休止的循环被切成一段段有名字的形状。人类的任何长期过程也被同样地切开，于是一段就是一个 phase。

senses.title: A period with a shared character
senses.titleCN: 时期：一段有共同特征的岁月
senses.definition: a period in a person's life or in history that has a particular character
senses.definitionCN: 个人生活或历史中具有某种共同特征的一段时间
senses.example: As a teenager he went through a rebellious phase.
senses.exampleCN: 十几岁时他经历过一段叛逆期。
senses.why: Here the slice is marked off not by an external schedule but by shared mood or behaviour. The boundary is drawn by likeness, not by a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这里的切片不是由外部日程划出的，而是由共同的情绪或行为划出的。界线由相似性决定，而非计划。

senses.title: The moon's apparent shape
senses.titleCN: 月相：月亮露出的那张脸
senses.definition: the shape of the moon or another planet as it appears to us at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 月亮或其他行星在某一时刻呈现给我们的形状
senses.example: A thin crescent is the phase just after the new moon.
senses.exampleCN: 细细的蛾眉月是新月之后的那个月相。
senses.why: This is the literal source. Greek phasis means appearance, and the moon is the thing whose appearance changes most visibly night after night.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义来源。希腊语 phasis 意为“显现”，而月亮正是夜复一夜外观变化最明显的那个东西。

senses.title: Physics: position in a wave cycle
senses.titleCN: 相位：波走到一圈的哪个位置
senses.definition: the point that a wave or oscillation has reached in its repeating cycle, measured as an angle
senses.definitionCN: 波或振动在重复循环中到达的位置，用角度来量度
senses.example: The two signals are in phase, so their peaks arrive together.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个信号同相，所以它们的波峰同时到达。
senses.why: A cycle can be drawn as a circle. Where you stand on that circle is your phase, so the moon idea becomes a measurable coordinate.
senses.whyCN: 一个循环可以画成一个圆。你站在那个圆上的位置就是相位，于是月亮的意象变成了可测量的坐标。

senses.title: Chemistry: a distinct state of matter
senses.titleCN: 相：同一条件下的一个物质状态
senses.definition: a state of matter, such as solid, liquid, or gas, that is distinct from other states present in the same system
senses.definitionCN: 同一体系中与其他状态明显不同的物质状态，如固、液、气
senses.example: Ice floating on water is a two-phase system.
senses.exampleCN: 浮在水上的冰构成一个两相体系。
senses.why: Inside one state the material is uniform, like one face of the moon. Crossing a visible boundary puts you in another phase.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个状态内部，物质是均匀的，就像月亮的同一张脸。越过一条可见的界线，就进入了另一个相。

senses.title: To carry out in planned stages
senses.titleCN: 分阶段实施：把整件事拆成几段来办
senses.definition: to organize an activity or change so that it happens in a series of planned stages
senses.definitionCN: 把一项活动或变革组织成一系列按计划推进的阶段
senses.example: The company will phase the new software into its offices over six months.
senses.exampleCN: 公司将在六个月内把新软件分阶段引入各个办公室。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: you treat a process as named slices and then perform the slices one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 名词动用：把过程当成一片片有名字的切片，再一片一片地执行。

senses.title: To introduce or remove gradually
senses.titleCN: 逐步引入／淘汰：一段一段地来
senses.definition: to bring something in or take it out gradually, stage by stage, instead of all at once
senses.definitionCN: 不是一次性，而是逐阶段地引入或撤出某物
senses.example: The old buses were phased out and replaced by electric ones.
senses.exampleCN: 旧公交车被逐步淘汰，换成了电动车。
senses.why: Phase in and phase out differ only in direction. Both keep every step small so that no single change is disruptive.
senses.whyCN: phase in 与 phase out 只差方向。两者都把每一步做小，使任何单次变化都不至于造成震荡。

senses.title: One aspect of a larger thing
senses.titleCN: 侧面：事物露给人的那一面
senses.definition: one part or aspect of a situation, especially the part that shows at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 一个情况的某一部分或某一方面，尤指某一时刻显露出来的那一面
senses.example: They studied only one phase of the problem, ignoring its economic side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们只研究了问题的一个侧面，忽略了其经济面。
senses.why: Phasis is appearance. Whatever shows itself at a given moment is one face of a larger object that has other faces.
senses.whyCN: phasis 是“显现”。在某一刻显现出来的，总是一个更大事物的其中一张脸，它还有别的脸。

intro.en: Phase began as an astronomer's word for the moon's changing face. From there it spread to any cycle cut into stages, and finally to any aspect of anything.
intro.cn: phase 起初是天文学家用来称月亮变换的脸的术语。由此扩及任何被切成阶段的循环，最后泛指任何事物的一个侧面。

items.en: Phainein meant 'to show, bring to light'. It comes from PIE *bha- 'to shine', the same family that gives English beacon and the Greek root behind phenomenon and emphasis.
items.cn: phainein 意为“显现、带到光下”。它来自原始印欧语 *bha-“发光”，同族词包括英语 beacon，以及 phenomenon、emphasis 背后的希腊词根。

items.en: From phainein came phasis, 'appearance', used especially of a star or the moon showing itself. The noun describes the act of appearing and the shape that appears.
items.cn: 由 phainein 生出 phasis“显现”，多用于星辰或月亮出现在天空中。这个名词既指显现的动作，也指显现出来的形状。

items.en: Greek astronomers spoke of the phases of the moon because its visible shape changes in a regular cycle. The term was technical before it was general.
items.cn: 希腊天文学家说月亮的 phases，因为它的可见形状按固定周期变化。这个词先是专业术语，后来才泛化。

items.en: Latin took phasis as a learned borrowing from Greek, keeping its astronomical sense. English received it through this Latin channel rather than directly.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 phasis 作为学术借词从希腊语引入，保留了天文学含义。英语是经这条拉丁渠道而非直接从希腊语接手的。

items.en: Phase of the moon is recorded in the 1660s. The general sense 'stage of development' appears in the 19th century, and the physics sense of wave phase follows in the same period.
items.cn: phase of the moon 的用法记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。“发展阶段”的泛义出现在 19 世纪，物理学上的“波相位”也同期出现。

items.en: Chemistry adopted phase for a distinct state of matter, and engineering adopted phase in and phase out for staged change. All of them keep the original picture: a cycle sliced into named parts.
items.cn: 化学用 phase 指一种独立的物质状态，工程领域用 phase in／phase out 指分阶段变更。这些用法都保留了原初画面：一个循环被切成有名字的几份。

note.en: The first group is built on near-identical spelling, only one of which shares the Greek root. The second group collects words for stages and aspects, each from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组拼写相近，其中只有一个与希腊词根同源。第二组收表示“阶段、方面”的词，但各自角度不同。

entries.definition: a group of words that forms a unit. It comes from Greek phrasis 'expression', from phrazein 'to point out, explain', not from phainein.
entries.definitionCN: 由一组词构成的单位。它来自希腊语 phrasis“表达”，动词 phrazein“指出、说明”，并非来自 phainein。

entries.definition: a rotating vector used to represent a wave, named directly from phase plus the -or agent ending.
entries.definitionCN: 用来表示波的旋转矢量，直接由 phase 加表施动者的 -or 构成。

entries.definition: arranged or carried out in stages. It is the past participle of the verb phase used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 按阶段安排或实施的。它是动词 phase 的过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: the gradual removal of something, formed from the verb phrase phase out.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步撤除某物，由动词短语 phase out 构成的复合名词。

entries.definition: a point or period in a process. Stage stresses the level reached, while phase stresses the bounded slice and often implies a cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 过程中的一个点或一段。stage 强调达到的程度，phase 强调有界的切片，且常含周期性。

entries.definition: a length of time with a defined beginning and end. Period is purely about time; phase also carries the idea of a distinct state or stage.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确起点和终点的一段时间。period 只谈时间；phase 还带有“独立状态或阶段”的意思。

entries.definition: one action in a sequence. A step is what you do; a phase is the stretch of time in which you do it.
entries.definitionCN: 序列中的一个动作。step 是你做的动作；phase 是做这件事的那段时间。

entries.definition: one part or feature of a situation. Aspect fits sense 08 closely; both come from roots meaning 'to look'.
entries.definitionCN: 情况的一个部分或特征。aspect 与第 8 义项最贴近，两者词根都含“看”的意思。

entries.definition: the condition something is in at a given time. State is static; phase is a position within a changing cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 某物在某一时刻所处的状况。state 是静态的；phase 是变化循环中的位置。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks: the moon, the sliced timeline, the in/out pair, the synchronized waves, and the face behind the Greek word.
normalIntro.cn: 五个具体抓手：月亮、被切分的时间轴、进与出的一对、同步的波、以及希腊词背后那张脸。

normal.en: PHASE = the moon's face. Picture eight named moons hanging on a string.
normal.cn: PHASE＝月亮的脸。想象八个有名字的月亮挂在一条绳上。

normal.en: Take a long timeline and cut it into thick slices. Each slice has a name; each name is a phase.
normal.cn: 把一条长长的时间轴切成厚片。每一片都有名字，每个名字就是一个 phase。

normal.en: Phase in: slices come in from the left. Phase out: slices leave to the right.
normal.cn: phase in：切片从左边进来；phase out：切片从右边退出。

normal.en: In phase means two waves raise their hands at the same moment. Out of phase means one is early.
normal.cn: in phase 是两个波在同一刻举手；out of phase 是一个来早了。

normal.en: Phase and face are cousins in meaning: both are about what shows. The moon changes face; we name its faces as phases.
normal.cn: phase 与 face 在意思上是亲戚：都关乎“显现出来的样子”。月亮换脸，我们把这些脸命名为 phase。

abstract.en: Any long thing can be treated as a circle cut into arcs; naming an arc is already a theory of the whole.
abstract.cn: 任何漫长之物都可以被看成切成弧段的圆；给一段弧命名，本身就已经是对整体的理论。

abstract.en: A phase is a frozen frame from a film that never stops running.
abstract.cn: 一个 phase 是从一部永不停机的电影里截下来的一帧。

abstract.en: Boundaries between phases are drawn by observers, not found in nature; the cycle only becomes usable when we cut it.
abstract.cn: 阶段之间的界线是观察者画的，不是自然里现成的；只有切开，循环才变得可用。

examples.en: The negotiation entered a delicate phase after both sides had stated their positions.
examples.cn: 双方陈述立场之后，谈判进入了一个微妙的阶段。

examples.en: Engineers check that the two generators remain in phase before connecting them to the grid.
examples.cn: 工程师在把两台发电机接入电网前，要确认它们保持同相。

examples.en: The city plans to phase out diesel buses by 2030, replacing them route by route.
examples.cn: 这座城市计划到 2030 年逐步淘汰柴油公交，按线路逐条替换。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费兹”听起来像 face（脸）——月亮一夜换一张脸，换出的每张脸就是一个 phase（月相、阶段）

root: 希腊语 phainein“显现、照亮”→ phasis“显现（月相）”→ 拉丁 phasis → 英语 phase；与 phenomenon、emphasis、fantasy 同一条 phan- 线。

sensesIntro.en: Start from the moon and move outward: one visible shape, then one stretch of a cycle, then one stretch of any process, then one aspect of anything. The verb adds the idea of doing the slices one at a time.
sensesIntro.cn: 从月亮出发向外推：先是一个可见形状，再是一个循环中的一段，再是任何过程的一段，最后是任何事物的一个侧面。动词义则加上“一片一片地做”的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full moon cycle divided into named arcs, each arc showing a different face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整轮月相循环被切成有名字的弧段，每段露出不同的脸。

chain: A CYCLE CUT INTO NAMED SLICES
ONE SLICE FROZEN AT A MOMENT

branches.en: TIME: a slice of a process and a stretch of life share one boundary-drawing gesture.
branches.cn: 时间：过程的一段与人生的一段，共用同一个划界动作。

branches.en: MOON: the literal origin, the visible face that gave the word its name.
branches.cn: 月亮：本义来源，那个让这个词得名的可见的脸。

branches.en: SCIENCE: wave position and state of matter both turn the slice into a measurable coordinate.
branches.cn: 科学：波的位置与物质状态，都把切片变成可测量的坐标。

branches.en: ACTION: doing the slices in order, inward or outward.
branches.cn: 行动：按顺序做这些切片，向内引入或向外撤出。

branches.en: ASPECT: whatever shows at one moment is one face of a larger thing.
branches.cn: 侧面：某一刻显现出来的，总是更大事物的其中一张脸。

intro.en: The phase family is built on one Greek verb of showing, with prefixes that locate the showing (above, through) and suffixes that turn it into nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: phase 词族建立在一个表示“显现”的希腊动词上，前缀标明显现的位置（在上、穿过），后缀把它变成名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed these Greek forms whole, so the same pieces appear in Latin scientific vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这些希腊形式整体借入，所以同样的构件也出现在拉丁科技术语里。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或状态的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 顿悟（某种东西在顶上显现）
透明的（光能穿过去显现）
阶段的（较少用，多为 phasic 替代）

definition_zh: 哲学；思想体系；人生准则；哲理；达观
definition_en: the study of the most basic questions about existence, knowledge, values, and reason; a system of ideas held by a person or group
core_image: 一个人放下手里的急事，转身追问「这一切究竟凭什么」
scene: 她的人生哲学很简单：努力工作，保持好奇。Her philosophy is simple: work hard and stay curious.
sceneCN: 这里 philosophy 是「一个人奉行的人生准则」（第 3 个义项：准则）；句意：她的人生准则很简单：努力工作，保持好奇。场景要点：不是学科、是一套自持的态度；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 哲学；思想体系；人生准则；达观

derivatives.zh: 哲学家；达观的人
哲学的；达观的
作哲学思考；空谈哲理
从哲学上；达观地

senses.title: The academic study of first questions
senses.titleCN: 哲学学科：追问最根本的问题
senses.definition: the academic study of the most basic questions about existence, knowledge, truth, values, and reason
senses.definitionCN: 对存在、知识、真理、价值与理性等最根本问题的学术研究
senses.example: She took up philosophy after a first course in logic.
senses.exampleCN: 上完一门逻辑学入门课之后，她开始研读哲学。
senses.why: The Greek word names a love of wisdom. A discipline that pursues wisdom for its own sake became a faculty, then a degree subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词本意是“爱智慧”。一门为智慧本身而追求智慧的学问，后来成了一个学科门类、一个学位专业。

senses.title: A system of thought
senses.titleCN: 思想体系：一套自成一体的说法
senses.definition: a particular system of ideas about the world, often named after its founder
senses.definitionCN: 关于世界的一套特定观念体系，常以其创立者命名
senses.example: His early work was shaped by German idealist philosophy.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的工作受到德国唯心主义哲学体系的影响。
senses.why: A discipline that keeps asking first questions produces rival answers. Each coherent set of answers becomes a philosophy with a name.
senses.whyCN: 一门不停追问根本问题的学科会产出彼此竞争的答案。每一套自洽的答案就变成了一个有名字的哲学体系。

senses.title: Guiding principles for living
senses.titleCN: 人生准则：拿来过日子的一套道理
senses.definition: the set of principles that guides a person's or an organization's behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指导个人或组织行为的一套原则
senses.example: Our philosophy is to fix the cause, not just the symptom.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的准则是解决病根，而不只是处理症状。
senses.why: The grand system shrinks to the scale of one life. What a person treats as first principles becomes their working philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的体系缩到一个人的尺度。一个人当作根本原则的东西，就成了他行事的准则。

senses.title: Calm acceptance of difficulty
senses.titleCN: 达观：把坏事放回它该有的尺寸
senses.definition: a calm attitude toward trouble, based on seeing it as part of a larger picture
senses.definitionCN: 面对困顿时的一种平静态度，源于把它看成更大图景的一部分
senses.example: He accepted the loss with philosophy and went back to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他达观地接受了损失，又回去工作了。
senses.why: The discipline trains you to see events against a wider frame. That habit, applied to daily misfortune, shows up as composure.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问训练你把事件放进更宽的框架里看。这个习惯用到日常的不幸上，表现出来就是沉着。

senses.title: The philosophy of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某领域的哲学：先问这门学问凭什么
senses.definition: the critical study of the assumptions and methods of a particular subject, such as science, law, or history
senses.definitionCN: 对某一学科（如科学、法律、历史）的前提与方法所作的批判性研究
senses.example: Philosophy of law asks what makes a rule legally valid.
senses.exampleCN: 法哲学追问：是什么使一条规则具有法律效力。
senses.why: Every field rests on assumptions it cannot prove from inside. Philosophy is called in to examine those foundations.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都建立在它内部无法证明的前提上。哲学被请来检查这些地基。

senses.title: The principles behind a practice
senses.titleCN: 理念：一套做法背后的道理
senses.definition: the set of ideas and aims that explain why something is done the way it is
senses.definitionCN: 解释某件事为何这样做的一套观念与目标
senses.example: The school's philosophy of teaching puts questions before answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校的教学理念把问题放在答案之前。
senses.why: Any practice can be asked for its rationale. The rationale, stated as principles, is its philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 任何做法都可以被追问理由。把这些理由表述为原则，就是它的理念。

senses.title: The ancient love of wisdom
senses.titleCN: 爱智：最早的那种生活方式
senses.definition: the original Greek pursuit of wisdom through reasoned inquiry, before it became an academic subject
senses.definitionCN: 希腊人最早通过理性探究追求智慧的生活方式，尚在它成为学科之前
senses.example: In Plato's dialogues, philosophy is a way of life rather than a job.
senses.exampleCN: 在柏拉图的对话里，哲学是一种生活方式而不是一份职业。
senses.why: Philosophia literally means love of wisdom. The historical sense keeps the desire rather than the syllabus.
senses.whyCN: philosophia 字面就是“爱智慧”。这个历史义保留的是那份渴望，而不是课程表。

senses.title: The habit of questioning assumptions
senses.titleCN: 追问前提：不接受「向来如此」
senses.definition: a critical habit of asking what an accepted belief rests on
senses.definitionCN: 一种批判性的习惯：追问一个被接受的看法究竟依托于什么
senses.example: Bring some philosophy to the meeting and ask why this rule exists.
senses.exampleCN: 带点哲学思辨进会场，问问这条规定为什么存在。
senses.why: Strip away the subject matter and what remains is a move: refuse to let a premise pass unexamined.
senses.whyCN: 剥掉具体内容，剩下的就是一个动作：不让任何一个前提未经检查就过关。

intro.en: Philosophy is a Greek compound meaning love of wisdom. The word names an attitude before it names a subject, and English borrowed it through Latin and French.
intro.cn: philosophy 是一个意为“爱智慧”的希腊复合词。它先命名的是一种态度，后来才命名一门学科；英语是经拉丁语和法语接手的。

items.en: Philos meant 'dear, beloved, loving'. It described affection and close friendship rather than abstract approval.
items.cn: philos 意为“亲爱的、被爱的、爱着的”。它描述的是亲近与友情，而不是抽象的赞同。

items.en: Sophia meant 'wisdom, skill, cleverness'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; some sources connect it with sophos 'wise' and possibly with words for clarity. This part of the chain is not firmly established.
items.cn: sophia 意为“智慧、技艺、聪明”。它更早的来源不确定；有说法把它与 sophos“智慧的”以及表示“清楚”的词联系起来。这一段词源链并无定论。

items.en: Philos plus sophia gave philosophia, 'the love of wisdom'. The word is associated with Pythagoras by later ancient reports, though the attribution is traditional rather than documented.
items.cn: philos 加 sophia 构成 philosophia“爱智慧”。后世古籍把这个词与毕达哥拉斯联系起来，但这属于传统说法，缺乏直接文献证据。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word unchanged in sense. Cicero and others used it for the Greek tradition of reasoned inquiry.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊词，含义不变。西塞罗等人用它来指希腊那条理性探究的传统。

items.en: Old French shortened and reshaped the word as filosofie, which is the form English received around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语把词形缩短、改造为 filosofie，英语约在 1300 年接受的就是这个形式。

items.en: From the 19th century the word also names a university department and its curriculum. The older sense of a way of life survives in phrases like with philosophy.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，这个词也指大学的院系及其课程。较古老的“生活方式”义则保存在 with philosophy 这类短语里。

note.en: The first group shares the philo- or soph- pieces but not always the whole meaning. The second group collects words for systems of belief.
note.cn: 第一组共享 philo- 或 soph- 构件，但未必整体同义。第二组收表示信仰体系的词。

entries.definition: a person who studies or practises philosophy. Philosophy plus -er, the person who loves wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或实践哲学的人。philosophy 加 -er，即爱智慧的人。

entries.definition: relating to philosophy, or calm in the face of trouble. The adjective covers both the academic and the composed senses.
entries.definitionCN: 与哲学有关的，或面对困顿时平静的。这个形容词同时覆盖学科义与达观义。

entries.definition: the study of language and texts historically. Philo- 'loving' plus logos 'word', so 'love of words', not love of wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 对语言与文本的历史研究。philo-“爱”加 logos“言词”，是“爱言词”，不是爱智慧。

entries.definition: clever but misleading argument. From sophos 'wise', but the word marks cleverness used to deceive rather than wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 巧妙却误导人的论证。源自 sophos“智慧的”，但这个词标记的是用于欺骗的机巧，而非智慧。

entries.definition: the activity or product of thinking. Thought is broader and looser; philosophy is organized and argues from principles.
entries.definitionCN: 思考活动或其产物。thought 更宽更松；philosophy 是有组织、从原则出发论证的。

entries.definition: a system of beliefs held by a group, often political. Ideology stresses shared social belief; philosophy stresses reasoned inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 群体持有的一套信念，常指政治的。ideology 强调群体共享的信念；philosophy 强调理性探究。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs taught by a religion or school. Doctrine is received and taught; philosophy invites challenge.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教或学派所传授的一套信念。doctrine 是被接受、被讲授的；philosophy 则欢迎质疑。

entries.definition: the overall way a person sees the world. Worldview can be unspoken and unexamined; philosophy is the examined version.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人看世界的总体方式。worldview 可以是未言明、未检查的；philosophy 是经过检查的版本。

entries.definition: the basic rules a person follows. Principles are the content; philosophy is the reasoned framework that holds them together.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人遵循的基本规则。principles 是内容；philosophy 是把它们统摄起来的理性框架。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the two Greek halves, the Pythagoras story, the difference from philology, the calm acceptance, and the meeting-room question.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：两个希腊半边、毕达哥拉斯的传说、与 philology 的区别、达观、以及会议室里的那一问。

normal.en: Philo- = loving, -sophy = wisdom. Philosophy is love of wisdom, spelled out in two halves.
normal.cn: philo-＝爱，-sophy＝智慧。philosophy 就是“爱智慧”，两个半边拼得明明白白。

normal.en: Pythagoras is said to have coined it: he called himself a lover of wisdom, not a possessor of it.
normal.cn: 据说毕达哥拉斯造了这个词：他称自己是智慧的热爱者，而不是占有者。

normal.en: Philology loves words, philosophy loves wisdom. Same prefix, different object.
normal.cn: philology 爱言词，philosophy 爱智慧。前缀相同，对象不同。

normal.en: With philosophy means carrying trouble lightly, as if it were one small item in a very large frame.
normal.cn: with philosophy 是把困顿拿得很轻，仿佛它只是一个极大画框里的小物件。

normal.en: In a meeting, philosophy is the person who asks why this rule exists at all.
normal.cn: 在会上，philosophy 就是那个问“这条规定到底为什么存在”的人。

abstract.en: Philosophy is what remains when you refuse to let any premise pass without asking what holds it up.
abstract.cn: 哲学就是当你拒绝让任何前提未经追问就过关时，剩下的那种活动。

abstract.en: A philosophy is a map of the whole drawn by someone who has never seen the whole.
abstract.cn: 一套哲学是一个从未见过整体的人画出的整体地图。

abstract.en: Wisdom is not a possession one can hold; the word's geometry is a reaching toward, not an arrival.
abstract.cn: 智慧不是可以握有的东西；这个词的几何形状是“伸向”，而不是“抵达”。

examples.en: He studied philosophy for four years before turning to artificial intelligence.
examples.cn: 他学了四年哲学，之后转向人工智能。

examples.en: Their company philosophy is that a slow correct decision beats a fast wrong one.
examples.cn: 他们的公司理念是：慢慢做对的决定胜过匆匆做错的决定。

examples.en: She took the criticism with philosophy and revised the paper that same week.
examples.cn: 她达观地接受了批评，并在同一周修改了论文。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费罗索菲”——费罗（philo，爱）追着索菲（sophia，智慧）跑，一路追问到底，就是哲学

root: 希腊语 philosophia＝philos“爱”+ sophia“智慧”；经拉丁 philosophia、古法语 filosofie 进入英语（约 1300 年）。sophia 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as an attitude (love of wisdom), hardens into a discipline, splits into rival systems, and then shrinks back down to one person's working principles or one field's foundations. The calm sense is the attitude applied to daily trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起于一种态度（爱智慧），固化为学科，分化为彼此竞争的体系，再缩回一个人的行事原则或一个领域的地基。达观义则是把这种态度用到日常困顿上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person setting down urgent business to ask what everything rests on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人放下急务，转去追问一切究竟依托于什么。

chain: A PERSONAL CREED OR FIELD S FOUNDATION

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the academic subject and the ancient way of life are the same pursuit, institutionalized or not.
branches.cn: 学科：学院里的科目与古代的生活方式是同一种追求，只是是否被制度化。

branches.en: SYSTEM: coherent answers harden into named schools.
branches.cn: 体系：自洽的答案凝固成有名字的学派。

branches.en: GUIDANCE: the grand system scaled down to a person's creed or an institution's rationale.
branches.cn: 指导：宏大体系缩到个人的准则或机构的理念。

branches.en: COMPOSURE: the wide frame applied to daily misfortune, which shows up as calm.
branches.cn: 达观：把宽框架用到日常不幸上，表现为平静。

branches.en: CRITIQUE: examining a field's assumptions, and the habit of refusing unexamined premises.
branches.cn: 批判：检查一个领域的前提，以及拒绝未经检查的前提这一习惯。
