senses.title: A baked dish with a pastry crust
senses.definition: a baked food consisting of a pastry crust that encloses a filling of meat, fruit, or vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 一种烤制的食物，酥皮外壳包裹着肉、水果或蔬菜做成的内馅
senses.example: She baked an apple pie for the family dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她为家庭晚餐烤了一个苹果派。
senses.why: The core image is a crust that completely wraps the filling, so the word first names the wrapped whole rather than the contents.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是酥皮把内馅整个包住，所以这个词首先指「包住的整体」，而不是里面的馅料。

senses.title: A sweet dessert pie
senses.definition: a pie whose filling is sweet, made with fruit, custard, or cream, served as dessert
senses.definitionCN: 内馅为甜味的派，用水果、蛋奶冻或奶油做成，作为甜点食用
senses.example: For dessert we had cherry pie with ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 甜点我们吃了樱桃派配冰淇淋。
senses.why: Once the pastry whole is the concept, the filling distinguishes subtypes, and sweet fillings became the default image in American English.
senses.whyCN: 既然「酥皮整体」已是概念核心，内馅便用来区分小类；甜馅在美式英语中成了默认画面，于是甜派独立成一个常用义项。

senses.title: A savoury meat pie
senses.definition: a pie filled with meat, gravy, or vegetables, eaten as a main dish or snack
senses.definitionCN: 以肉、肉汁或蔬菜为馅的派，可当主食或点心
senses.example: He bought a hot meat pie at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在车站买了一个热乎的肉馅饼。
senses.why: The same wrapped-whole image works for savoury fillings, and this is the older, especially British, everyday sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「包裹的整体」这一意象同样适用于咸馅；咸派是这个词更古老、尤其在英国更日常的义项。

senses.title: A whole divided into shares
senses.definition: something regarded as a whole amount of money, power, or benefit that can be divided among people
senses.definitionCN: 被看作一笔钱、一份权力或一批好处，可以在人们之间切分的整体
senses.example: Both firms want a bigger slice of the profit pie.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司都想从利润这块大蛋糕里分到更大的一块。
senses.why: A round pie is naturally cut into slices, so the image extends to any whole whose parts are shares fought over by claimants.
senses.whyCN: 圆派天然要切成块，这一画面便延伸到任何可以被切分、且各方争抢份额的整体，如利润、市场或预算。

senses.title: A circular statistical diagram
senses.definition: a circle divided into sectors, each showing the proportion of one part of a whole, as in a pie chart
senses.definitionCN: 被分成若干扇形的圆，每个扇形表示整体中某一部分所占比例，用于饼图
senses.example: The report shows spending in a pie chart.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用饼图展示了各项支出。
senses.why: Because the divided-pie image already means a whole split into shares, statisticians borrowed it for a circle cut into proportional sectors.
senses.whyCN: 既然「切分的派」已表示「整体分成份额」，统计学家便借用了这幅画面，把分成比例扇形的圆叫作饼图。

senses.title: Something very easy
senses.definition: something very easy to do, as in the informal phrase as easy as pie
senses.definitionCN: 非常容易做到的事，见于非正式短语 as easy as pie（易如反掌）
senses.example: Don't worry, the test is as easy as pie.
senses.exampleCN: 别担心，这次考试易如反掌。
senses.why: Eating a pie is pleasant and takes no skill, so the phrase came to describe tasks as effortless as enjoying dessert.
senses.whyCN: 吃派轻松愉快、不需要任何技巧，于是这个说法被用来形容像吃甜点一样毫不费劲的任务。

senses.title: A false or empty promise
senses.definition: a promised benefit that is unrealistic and will never arrive, as in pie in the sky
senses.definitionCN: 不切实际、永远不会兑现的许诺，见于短语 pie in the sky（空中馅饼；空头支票）
senses.example: Their pledge of free housing is just pie in the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 他们免费住房的承诺不过是空中馅饼。
senses.why: A pie floating in the sky can be seen but never eaten, so the image names a reward that is dangled yet permanently out of reach.
senses.whyCN: 挂在天上的派看得见却永远吃不着，这幅画面正好用来命名那种被许诺出来、却始终够不到的好处。

senses.title: An affectionate term for a person
senses.definition: used affectionately of a person one loves, as in sweetie pie or cutie pie
senses.definitionCN: 用于亲昵称呼所爱的人，如 sweetie pie、cutie pie（甜心、宝贝）
senses.example: Come here, sweetie pie, and give me a hug.
senses.exampleCN: 过来，小甜心，抱一个。
senses.why: Something sweet and whole and shared within the family becomes a metaphor for a beloved person, sweet as dessert and dear as home.
senses.whyCN: 甜的、圆满的、全家人分享的东西，被用来比喻所爱的人：像甜点一样甜，像家常一样亲。

intro.en: The word pie was first recorded in English in the late 13th century as a name for the pastry dish, but its ultimate origin is uncertain; the most discussed theory links it to the bird name pie (magpie), from Latin pica.
intro.cn: pie 一词在十三世纪末的英语中首次被记录为这种酥皮点心的名称，但其最终来源不确定；被讨论最多的一种假说是把它与鸟名 pie（喜鹊）联系起来，该鸟名来自拉丁语 pica。

items.en: First attested as 'pie', a pastry case with a filling; the earliest records give no derivation, so the source is generally treated as uncertain.
items.cn: 最早以 pie 的形式出现，指带馅的酥皮点心；最早期的文献没有给出词源说明，因此一般认为来源不确定。

items.en: The bird name pie (as in magpie) goes back to Latin pica 'magpie'; some scholars suggest the dish was named after the bird because its assorted fillings resembled the magpie's habit of collecting all kinds of things, though this link is not proven.
items.cn: 鸟名 pie（见 magpie）可追溯到拉丁语 pica「喜鹊」；一些学者认为点心因馅料五花八门、像喜鹊什么都收集而得名，但这一联系并未被证实。

items.en: Early recipes describe pies as pastry coffins enclosing meat, fish, or fruit, confirming that the defining idea was the enclosing crust rather than any particular ingredient.
items.cn: 早期食谱把派描述为包裹肉、鱼或水果的「酥皮棺盒」，说明其定义性特征是包裹用的酥皮，而非某种特定馅料。

items.en: Figurative uses spread: the divided pie as an image of shared benefits, and the phrase humble pie, a folk-etymological reshaping of 'umble pie' made from offal.
items.cn: 比喻用法扩展：被切分的派成为分享利益的意象；humble pie 则是由 umble pie（用内脏做的派）经民间词源改造而来。

items.en: Compounds and idioms consolidated: pie chart (20th c.), pie in the sky (from a 1911 labour song), as easy as pie, and sweetie pie as a term of endearment.
items.cn: 复合词与习语定型：pie chart（二十世纪）、pie in the sky（出自一九一一年的劳工歌曲）、as easy as pie，以及用作爱称的 sweetie pie。

note.en: Watch out for the short-vowel words that look or sound like pie, and for the pastry words that share its meaning field.
note.cn: 注意与 pie 拼写或发音相近的短元音词，以及与它同处「糕点」义场的词。

entries.definition: a structure built out over water so ships can load and unload, or for people to walk on
entries.definitionCN: 突堤码头；水上平台；只是与 pie 拼写相近（多一个 r），词源不同

entries.definition: a farm animal with a snout, kept for its meat
entries.definitionCN: 猪；只是拼形相近，与 pie 无词源关联

entries.definition: to fasten with string or rope, or a strip of cloth worn round the neck
entries.definitionCN: 系；领带；与 pie 同押 /aɪ/ 音但词源无关

entries.definition: a black-and-white bird known for collecting shiny objects; figuratively a hoarder
entries.definitionCN: 喜鹊；由 mag 加 pie 构成的复合词，被认为是 pie 的可能词源线索

entries.definition: an open pastry case with a filling but no top crust
entries.definitionCN: 果馅饼；挞；与 pie 同类，但通常无上层酥皮

entries.definition: dough made of flour, fat and water used as the base or covering of baked foods
entries.definitionCN: 油酥面团；酥皮糕点；pie 的外壳正是用 pastry 做的

entries.definition: an open savoury flan of pastry filled with eggs, cream and other foods
entries.definitionCN: 法式咸派（乳蛋饼）；义场与咸派相近

entries.definition: a sweet baked food made from flour, sugar and eggs
entries.definitionCN: 蛋糕；同为甜烤食品，但无酥皮包裹内馅的结构

entries.definition: a dish of food cooked slowly in a covered pot, or the covered pot itself
entries.definitionCN: 砂锅炖菜；同为「包裹式」的家常整份食物，但用锅而非酥皮

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks built on the word's sounds, compounds and idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 五个记忆钩子，建立在发音、复合词与习语之上。

normal.en: pie /paɪ/ rhymes with 'buy': you buy a pie at the bakery.
normal.cn: pie 与 buy 押韵：在面包店 buy（买）一块 pie（派）。

normal.en: magpie keeps the ending pie: the bird that collects everything, like a pie collecting all kinds of fillings.
normal.cn: magpie（喜鹊）以 pie 结尾：什么都收集的鸟，正如派什么馅都装。

normal.en: pie chart: a circle cut like a pie, each slice a percentage.
normal.cn: pie chart（饼图）：把圆像派一样切开，每块是一个百分比。

normal.en: as easy as pie: eating pie takes no skill, so the task is effortless.
normal.cn: as easy as pie：吃派毫不费劲，所以事情易如反掌。

normal.en: a slice of the pie: profits are the pie, your share is one slice.
normal.cn: a slice of the pie：利润是整张派，你的份额是其中一块。

abstract.en: Picture a golden crust as a lid that seals a treasure of filling underneath.
abstract.cn: 把金黄酥皮想成一个盖子，封住下面满满一盆宝藏般的内馅。

abstract.en: See the whole pie as a coin of benefit: whoever holds the knife decides who eats.
abstract.cn: 把整张派想象成一枚利益硬币：谁握着刀，谁就决定谁有得吃。

abstract.en: Imagine a pie floating in the sky: you can see it, but you can never bite it — a promise that never lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一块派漂在天上：看得见却咬不着——一个永远不会落地的承诺。

examples.en: Mom baked an apple pie and the whole house smelled of cinnamon.
examples.cn: 妈妈烤了一个苹果派，满屋子都是肉桂的香气。

examples.en: The engineers demanded a fair share of the bonus pie.
examples.cn: 工程师们要求在奖金这块蛋糕里分得公平的一块。

examples.en: The budget is shown as a pie chart on the second page.
examples.cn: 预算在第二页用一张饼图来展示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派」——pie 的发音正像中文的「派」：一块圆饼切开分派给大家，谁都得「派」一块；分派、派送的画面帮助锁定「可分的整体」这层意思。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为 pie 首见于十三世纪末的中古英语，指带馅的酥皮点心；最常见的假说是与鸟名 pie（见 magpie，源自拉丁语 pica「喜鹊」）有关——因派的馅料五花八门，类似喜鹊什么都收集的习性，但此说未被证实，应视为存疑的联想而非定论。

sensesIntro.en: From the concrete pastry whole, the word extends to its sweet and savoury subtypes, then figuratively to any divisible whole, its statistical diagram, and idioms for ease and empty promises.
sensesIntro.cn: 从具体的「酥皮包裹的整份食物」出发，先分出甜、咸两个小类，再比喻为任何可切分的整体，进而延伸到统计图示，以及表示「轻而易举」与「空头许诺」的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a golden crust sealing a full filling, cut into slices to be shared
core.cn: 核心意象：金黄酥皮封住满满内馅，切开分食

branches.en: The baked dish itself: crust plus filling as one whole.
branches.cn: 烤制的食物本身：酥皮加内馅构成一个整体。

branches.en: The filling decides the subtype: sweet dessert or savoury meat pie.
branches.cn: 内馅决定小类：甜点派或咸味肉派。

branches.en: The pie cut into slices stands for any divisible whole, including the statistical pie chart.
branches.cn: 被切分的派代表任何可分的整体，包括统计上的饼图。

branches.en: Eating pie is easy and sweet, giving the idioms for easy tasks and affectionate names.
branches.cn: 吃派轻松又甜，由此产生形容「易如反掌」的习语和亲昵的爱称。

branches.en: A pie in the sky can be seen but never eaten: the empty promise.
branches.cn: 天上的派看得见吃不着：空头许诺。

intro.en: pie has no certain root or affix of its own; its word family is built almost entirely from compounds and idioms.
intro.cn: pie 本身没有确定的词根或词缀；它的词族几乎全部由复合词和习语构成。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin-shaped lead is pica, the bird name behind magpie, which some scholars connect to the dish — an unproven hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 唯一带拉丁色彩的线索是 pica，即 magpie 一词背后的鸟名，有学者把它与这种点心联系起来——但这是未被证实的假说。

items.meaning: a black-and-white bird that collects shiny things; a hoarder
items.meaningCN: 喜鹊；爱收集亮东西的鸟，比喻囤积杂物的人
items.example: She is a magpie for old postcards.
items.exampleCN: 她对旧明信片见一面就收。

items.meaning: the pastry shell of a pie
items.example: Roll the pie crust thin and even.

items.meaning: a sweet pie filled with apples; a symbol of traditional home values
items.meaningCN: 苹果派；美式家庭传统的象征
items.example: Nothing beats warm apple pie with cream.
items.exampleCN: 没什么能比得上热苹果派配奶油。

items.meaning: a savoury pie filled with meat and gravy
items.meaningCN: 肉馅饼；以肉和肉汁为馅的咸派
items.example: He grabbed a meat pie on his way to work.
items.exampleCN: 他上班路上顺手买了个肉馅饼。

items.meaning: a circle divided into sectors showing proportions
items.meaningCN: 饼图；分成扇形以显示比例的圆形统计图
items.example: Draw a pie chart of the monthly costs.
items.exampleCN: 画一张每月开支的饼图。

items.meaning: an empty promise of future rewards
items.example: Higher pay for longer hours is pie in the sky.
items.exampleCN: 工时更长还指望加薪，那是空中馅饼。

items.example: The recipe is as easy as pie.

items.meaning: a term of endearment for a loved person
humiliation, especially having to admit one's error
items.example: He had to eat humble pie and apologise.
items.exampleCN: 他只好低头认错并道歉。

latinEntries.meaning: magpie; proposed but unproven source of the bird name pie
latinEntries.meaningCN: 喜鹊；被提出作为鸟名 pie 的来源，但未经证实
latinEntries.example: Latin pica survives in the scientific name Pica pica for the magpie.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pica 保留在喜鹊的学名 Pica pica 中。

derivatives.zh: 由 mag 加 pie 构成的复合名词，义为「喜鹊；爱收集杂物的人」
由 sweetie 加 pie 构成的爱称，义为「甜心；宝贝」

definition_zh: 一块；一片；一件；作品；棋子；拼合
definition_en: a part cut or broken from something larger; a single work of art or music; one of the objects moved in a board game; to join parts into a whole
core_image: 一块带釉的碎瓷片躺在桌上，断口处仍泛着光
scene: 搬家那天，纸箱落地，一只旧碗碎成几块，最大的那块还带着半圈蓝花。She picked up the largest piece and turned it over in her hand.
sceneCN: 这里 piece 指「一块、一片」（第 1 个义项：从整体上分下来的一部分）；句意为她捡起最大的那一块，在手里翻看。图中可辨识物件：碎瓷片、蓝花、落地的纸箱。

pos.zh: 一块；一片；一件；作品；棋子

derivatives.zh: 由 piece 加古英语后缀 -meal（逐……地）构成，义为「一件一件的；零碎的」
由 a 与 piece 合成，义为「每人；各」
由 master 与 piece 复合而成，义为「杰作」

senses.title: A part broken or cut from something larger
senses.definition: a part separated from a whole, especially one small enough to hold or to see as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 从整体上分离出来的一部分，尤指小到可以拿在手里或单独看见的一块
senses.example: She picked up the largest piece of the broken bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她捡起碎碗上最大的那一块。
senses.why: Medieval Latin petia named a fragment, and English took the word with that broken-off shape already inside it, so the first sense is the shard rather than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 本指碎片，英语借来时，「从整体上断下来的一块」这个形状已经装在词里，所以最早的义项是碎片而非整体。

senses.title: A single work of art, music, or writing
senses.definition: one complete work, especially a short musical composition, a painting, or a short text
senses.definitionCN: 一件完整的作品，尤指短小的乐曲、一幅画或一段短文
senses.example: The band played a new piece at the end of the set.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在演出末尾演奏了一首新作品。
senses.why: A work is also a unit that can be counted and handed over, so the noun that counted fragments came to count finished works, each treated as one whole.
senses.whyCN: 作品同样是可以清点、可以交到别人手里的一个单位，于是原本数碎块的名词也用来数成品，每一件都被当作一个整体。

senses.title: One of the objects moved in a board game
senses.definition: one of the small objects that a player moves on a board, as in chess or draughts
senses.definitionCN: 棋手在棋盘上移动的小物件之一，如国际象棋或跳棋中的棋子
senses.example: He moved a single piece and the whole game turned.
senses.exampleCN: 他挪动了一枚棋子，整盘棋就变了。
senses.why: A game set is a collection of small separate units, and each one is literally a piece taken out of the box, which is why the word needed no stretching here.
senses.whyCN: 一副棋就是一小堆彼此分开的小单位，每一枚本来就是从盒子里取出来的一块，所以这个词在这里根本不必引申。

senses.title: To join parts into a whole
senses.definition: to put the separate parts of something together until they form a whole, often by patient work
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分开的各个部分合在一起，直到形成整体，常需耐心
senses.example: They pieced the torn map back together on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在地板上把撕破的地图重新拼好。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: what was broken into pieces is put back, and the word now watches the fragments travel toward a whole instead of away from it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的方向倒过来：被分成块的东西重新合起来，这个词现在看着碎块朝整体走，而不是从整体散开。

intro.en: Piece came through Old French from a medieval Latin word for a fragment, and that word's own earlier origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: piece 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语中表示碎片的一个词，而那个词更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin petia or petium meant a piece or fragment, but its earlier origin is uncertain and a Gaulish source is often suggested.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 或 petium 意为一块、碎片，但它更早的来源不确定，常有人推测来自高卢语。

items.en: Old French piece named a part, a fragment, or a coin, and carried the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 piece 指一部分、碎片或一枚钱币，诺曼时期之后把这个词带进英语。

items.en: Middle English piece could mean a fragment, a share, or a particular item, and the spelling settled without the French accent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 piece 可指碎片、份额或某一件事物，拼写逐渐定型，去掉了法语的变音记号。

items.en: By the sixteenth century a piece could be a work of art or music, because such a work is exactly one countable item.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，piece 已可指一件艺术品或一首乐曲，因为这样一件作品恰好就是一个可以清点的事项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the fragment at the centre and builds phrasal verbs such as piece together, where the fragments are put back.
items.cn: 现代英语仍以碎片为中心，并造出 piece together 这类短语动词，让碎片重新拼回去。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the same stem plus two words that only share the sound or the spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for parts and fragments.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式，外加两个只在发音或拼写上相近的词；近义组收表示部分与碎片的词。

entries.definition: Done in separate stages or small amounts rather than all at once.
entries.definitionCN: 分成若干阶段或小份来做，而非一次完成。

entries.definition: For each person or thing; one to each.
entries.definitionCN: 每人或每件各一个。

entries.definition: A state of quiet and freedom from war; it sounds the same but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 没有战争与纷扰的安宁状态；发音相同，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To make a hole through something with a sharp point; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用尖物在物体上穿出孔洞；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small part broken off from something.
entries.definitionCN: 从某物上断下的一小块。

entries.definition: A part of something larger, often a share given to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 较大事物的一部分，常指分给某人的份额。

entries.definition: A small piece or amount of something.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块或少量。

entries.definition: One of the parts into which something is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被分成的若干部分之一。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from a fragment, and its family keeps counting parts, works, and small movable units.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从碎片出发，它的词族一直在数部分、作品和可以移动的小单位。

normal.en: Piece came from Old French, and the medieval Latin form behind it already meant a fragment.
normal.cn: piece 来自古法语，而它背后的中世纪拉丁语形式本就已经指碎片。

normal.en: Piece together is the noun turned into a verb: the fragments are made to travel back into a whole.
normal.cn: piece together 是名词转成动词：碎块被赶回整体里去。

normal.en: Peace sounds exactly the same but comes from a different root, so the two must be kept apart in writing.
normal.cn: peace 读音完全相同，但来自另一个词根，所以写的时候必须把两者分开。

normal.en: Apiece adds a to piece and means one for each, as in tickets at ten pounds apiece.
normal.cn: apiece 在 piece 前加 a，意为「每人一个」，如门票每张十英镑。

normal.en: A piece of music and a piece of news both use piece as a counter for one item, not as a fragment.
normal.cn: 「一首乐曲」与「一则消息」里的 piece 都是清点事项的量词用法，而不是碎片。

abstract.en: The same word counts a broken shard, a finished sonata and a chessman, because English counts parts and wholes with one noun.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既数碎瓷片，也数写完的奏鸣曲和一枚棋子，因为英语用一个名词同时数部分与整体。

abstract.en: To piece something together is to trust that the fragments still carry the shape of what they came from.
abstract.cn: 把东西拼起来，就是相信这些碎片仍然带着它们原来所属之物的形状。

abstract.en: A piece is always smaller than its whole, except when the whole is a work of art, and then the piece is the whole.
abstract.cn: 一块总比它的整体小，除非那个整体是一件作品，这时「一件」就等于整体。

examples.en: She picked up the largest piece of the broken bowl.
examples.cn: 她捡起碎碗上最大的那一块。

examples.en: They pieced the torn map back together on the floor.
examples.cn: 他们在地板上把撕破的地图重新拼好。

examples.en: He moved one piece and the game changed.
examples.cn: 他挪动了一枚棋子，整盘棋就变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈死」——碗被劈成几块，一块就是 a piece；记住 piece 是碎片、一块。

root: 古法语 piece 来自中世纪拉丁语 petia 或 petium（一块、碎片），更早来源不确定，常推测与高卢语有关；没有可靠的古典拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a part separated from a whole; from that one shard grow the countable work, the chessman, and the verb that puts fragments back together.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从整体上分下来的一块；由这一块碎片长出可清点的作品、棋盘上的棋子，以及把碎块拼回整体的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shard of glazed china lying on a table, its broken edge still shining.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块带釉的碎瓷片躺在桌上，断口处仍泛着光。

branches.en: a shard of blue-patterned china on the floor
branches.cn: 地上一块带蓝花的瓷片

branches.en: a short piano work printed on a single page
branches.cn: 印在一页纸上的短小钢琴曲

branches.en: a chessman lifted between two fingers
branches.cn: 两根手指夹起的一枚棋子

branches.en: a torn map spread out and matched edge to edge
branches.cn: 摊开的地图被一处处对上边

branches.en: a bowl repaired with visible seams
branches.cn: 用看得见的接缝补好的碗

intro.en: There is no classical Latin root to lean on here, so the entries follow the medieval Latin noun, its French form, and the English compounds built on it.
intro.cn: 这里没有可依托的古典拉丁词根，所以这些条目沿着中世纪拉丁语名词、它的法语形式，以及在其上构成的英语复合词排列。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin form in the record is the medieval petia, whose own origin is uncertain, so this entry is short and cautious.
latinIntro.cn: 记录中唯一的拉丁形式是中世纪拉丁语的 petia，它自身的来源并不确定，所以这一条列得简短而谨慎。
